News.title: What time do A-level results come out today? When to get your grades on results day 2026 and how to collect them
News.content:
HUNDREDS of thousands of teenagers across the UK are bracing for a nerve-racking morning on A-level results day.

Here is all you need to know about what happens on the day, and how to collect your grades.

When do A-level results come out?

This year, A-level results day falls on Thursday, August 13.



The Joint Council for Qualifications sets the date and it applies across every exam board, including AQA, Pearson Edexcel, OCR, WJEC and CCEA in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.



This covers AS Levels, the Extended Project, free-standing maths qualifications, as well as Level 3 applied and vocational technical qualifications.

OCR’s Cambridge Technicals at Level 2 and Level 3 can be issued to students slightly earlier from Monday, August 10, but schools and colleges can choose to hold them back until the main results days.

Exams officers can see results on their systems from 12.01am, but they can only give results slips to students from 8am.



Bear in mind that 8am is the earliest permitted time results can be handed out – not a fixed release time.

Each school or college has its own specific policy on when and how students can collect their results.

How do I collect A-level results?

There are several options available for how you can collect your grades on the results day:

In person: Go to your school or college with your photo ID to collect a printed slip with your results. If you personally cannot attend, give your institution a written letter naming your proxy with their ID to collect your results for you.

Go to your school or college with your photo ID to collect a printed slip with your results. If you personally cannot attend, give your institution a written letter naming your proxy with their ID to collect your results for you. Online: Log into your institution’s online portal to view your grades. Most results are sent to UCAS and your chosen universities or colleges automatically, so you can also use the UCAS Hub to see if your university place is confirmed, but this will not show raw grades.

Log into your institution’s online portal to view your grades. Most results are sent to UCAS and your chosen universities or colleges automatically, so you can also use the UCAS Hub to see if your university place is confirmed, but this will not show raw grades. Email or post: Check your email inbox, including the spam folder, if your institution sends digital copies. Some schools mail physical copies if arranged beforehand.

Schools and colleges set their own arrangements, with some handing out printed slips in person while others use online portals or email, so it is worth checking your specific institution’s policy.



Can you challenge an A-Level grade?

The request to review marking must come from the school or college itself, so you will have to speak to your exams officer should you wish to challenge your grades.

If they refuse to ask for a review, you are entitled to use the school’s internal appeals procedure to challenge that refusal.

A review can push a mark down as well as up, which is why the student has to give written consent and the school has to keep it on file.

There may also be a fee if the grade does not change, so it is a good idea to check what it costs first.

If a university or further education place hangs on the outcome, the cut-off for a priority review is August 20, otherwise the standard deadline is September 24.



When the exam board sends out the result of your review, you have 30 days from that date to appeal it.

An appeal has two stages – if you are unhappy with the first answer, you have another 14 days to ask for a hearing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you have asked for a review that could change your grade, tell the university straight away.

The exam board does not tell Ucas or the university that a review is underway, but it will report any grade change that comes out of it, and the university is under no obligation to hold your place in the meantime.

News.title: What time does Ucas Hub update on A-level results day 2026? When to check the status of your university offers
News.content:
STUDENTS will soon find out whether they have secured a place at their preferred university, with A-level results just around the corner.

Thursday, August 12, is results day for hundreds of thousands of teenagers – and for those seeking to remain in education, Ucas plays a big part of proceedings.

What is the difference between A-level results and a Ucas score?

A-level results are the traditional letter grades from A* to E that students receive from your exam boards.



Ucas score, also called tariff points, is a numerical value assigned to those letter grades, allowing universities to compare different types of qualifications equally.



Each letter grade you achieve in a full A-level translates into a specific number of UCAS points:

A*: 56 points

56 points A: 48 points

48 points B: 40 points

40 points C: 32 points

32 points D: 24 points

24 points E: 16 points

Your total Ucas score is calculated by adding the points of all your eligible qualifications together.

Your total Ucas score can also include points from other qualifications outside of your A-levels, such as Extended Project, AS-levels, T-levels, BTECs or music exams.



You can use the official Ucas calculator to total up your projected score.

What time does the Ucas Hub update on A-level results day 2026?

Students will be able to access their applications from 8am when the embargo is lifted.

Individual records typically process across the system between 8am and 8.15am.

However, with thousands of students logging in simultaneously, expect slow loading and be patient.



Avoid refreshing the page constantly, as this could worsen server traffic.

The Ucas customer experience centre phone lines open at 8.30am if you need direct troubleshooting assistance.

The Ucas Hub tells you where you stand with your firm and insurance university choices.

It will not show your actual grades – those only come from your school or college.

It could show one of the following outcomes:



Your place at your first choice is confirmed

You have been placed at your backup

You have been offered a changed course, which might mean a different course, a different start date or a different point of entry

Your application is still awaiting a decision

You are eligible for Clearing

You then need to check the details of the offer and do what the university asks, which may include proving your qualifications or meeting any outstanding conditions.

A changed-course offer requires a quick decision – you normally have five days to accept or decline, and letting it sit could cost you the place.

Awaiting a decision does not mean you have been rejected.

Universities sometimes take students who have narrowly missed an offer, so it is worth getting on the phone.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Students can only use Clearing once their status says they are eligible, or when they have formally declined or released themselves from a place they are holding.



Clearing choices will become available to students from 1pm on results day.

News.title: Dad charged with murder of daughter Minnie Merriman, 9, in Arbroath due in court today
News.content:
A DAD charged with murdering nine-year-old schoolgirl Minnie Merriman in Arbroath is due to appear in court again today.

Christopher Rice, 35, is alleged to have killed his daughter, who was found seriously injured at an industrial estate in the town on August 3.



He was charged in connection with her alleged murder and initially appeared at Forfar Sheriff Court last week.

Rice, from West Yorkshire, was led into the court in cuffs by officers on August 5.



He made no plea and was remanded in custody.

He is expected to return to the dock today, August 13, for a private hearing.

Minnie had been on a family camping trip when she was found fatally injured shortly after midnight on August 3.

Emergency services raced to the Elliot Industrial Estate after the alarm was raised and the youngster was rushed to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where she later died.

We previously reported how Minnie was discovered after the family’s camping trip led them to pitch a tent within the estate.

Witnesses told of their surprise at the family’s makeshift campsite, less than a mile from the seafront, after they were seen cooking on an outdoor stove just hours before Minnie was found injured.



Minnie was rushed to hospital along with three other patients before she died.

In a tribute following her death Minnie’s devastated family described her as their “beautiful and brave Minnie Moo”.

Minnie’s heartbroken mum Laurie Eve Merriman left a devastating tribute at the scene in the days that followed, saying she will be “eternally connected” to her daughter.

A note from the mum read: “To my darling Minnie Moo.

“Wherever you are, we’re still connected eternally.



“I love you my girl.

“Mammy will carry your strength always.”

More to follow…

For the latest news on this story keep checking back at The Scottish Sun.

News.title: Girl, 16, rushed to hospital with ‘serious’ stab wounds at a home as woman, 45, arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'KNIFE' ATTACK Girl, 16, rushed to hospital with ‘serious’ stab wounds at a home as woman, 45, arrested

A TEENAGE girl was rushed to hospital with “serious” stab wounds – and a woman has been arrested.

Emergency services scrambled to a residential address in Coventry, West Midlands, on Tuesday evening, where they found a 16-year-old girl with a stab wound, as well as a woman, 42, with minor injuries.

A 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of two counts of wounding and remains in custody.

Police have described the incident as “isolated” and officers will be in the Henley Green area of the city to “offer reassurance”.





A spokesman for West Midlands Police said yesterday: “We were called to Roselands Avenue at around 10.10pm last night to reports of a stabbing.

“A 16-year-old girl was taken to hospital with a stab wound and has since been discharged.

“A 42-year-old woman with minor injuries was also taken to hospital and has also been discharged.

“A 45-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of two counts of wounding and remains in police custody.



“We understand that the community will be worried by this news.

“We can confirm that it was an isolated incident, but we will have officers in the local area to offer reassurance.”

News.title: Girl, 1, killed and student missing after deadly hippo attack as huge beast overturns canoe in river
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

RIVER TRAGEDY Girl, 1, killed and student missing after deadly hippo attack as huge beast overturns canoe in river

A RAGING hippo has attacked a canoe and killed a one-year-old girl with another young student still missing.

The canoe was carrying 18 farmers and children when it capsized in Kenya’s longest river following a violent assault from the huge hippo.



A routine crossing of the Tana River quickly turned tragic on Tuesday with 16 people quickly rescued from the water after the attack at Mikinduni Village.

Police said the canoe capsized after a hippopotamus attacked the passengers.



A 20-month-old girl drowned in the river while another passenger was unaccounted for when rescuers pulled everyone from the water.

Police said the baby’s body was recovered and taken to the mortuary at Hola County Referral Hospital for a postmortem exam.



Officials believe the missing child is a Form Three student which in Kenya would make the girl aged 16 or 17.

The Chanani Secondary School student is still yet to be found.

Hippo attacks are common in the area despite regular crossings taking place at Tana River.

It comes just days after terrifying footage showed a hippo charging at a boat packed with tourists.



Viral footage captured the heart-stopping moment the massive beast suddenly gave chase in Botswana, forcing the fleeing boat to speed away.

The person filming the chilling encounter said: “For a few moments, every single person in the boat was genuinely worried.”

Another described the moment as “one of the most terrifying moments he’d ever experienced”.

Hippos kill an estimated 500 people each year in Africa.

This makes them one of the world’s deadliest land mammals and more dangerous than lions and elephants to humans.

News.title: Sick tactics of Thai mafia with £200 hitmen, £11 grenades & girls sold into sex trade by dads…as innocent Brits targeted
News.content:
IT’S known as the “land of smiles” with more than a million Brits visiting Thailand every year.

But a dark cloud hangs over the backpacker destination as crime gangs target tourists in cheap cons and the country is dogged by claims of mafia rule.



The Sun can today reveal the truth behind the Thai gangs who carry out £200 hits on mopeds, sell hand grenades for £11 and encourage poverty-stricken families to sell their daughters into the sex trade.

One Brit claimed he was tricked out of £100,000 and suffered sinister threats after setting up business in the Asian country and is now reliant on GoFundMe donations. While an ex-drug smuggler lifted the lid on how weapons stolen from military and police armouries are sold on the streets for a few hundred pounds.

Thailand has long denied it has a criminal gang problem but rumours of the Thai mafia first drew attention back in 2014 when the disfigured bodies of British backpackers David Miller, 24, and Hannah Witheridge, 23, were discovered on party island Koh Tao.



At the time, local police insisted there was “100 per cent” no mafia, yet plans to raid “influential rackets and illegitimate businesses” were announced.

But David’s terrified pal Sean McAnna, then 25, claimed the “Thai mafia are trying to kill me” after unknowingly meeting mobsters in a bar, who tried to pressure him to take the rap for the murders and threatened: “You die tonight.”

Sean, a Scottish busker, fled from the islands fearing for his life. And since that terrifying incident more crimes linked to organised crime groups have emerged.

When local taxi driver Sikharin Promcharoen, 31, was beaten-up and fatally shot six times in June, after dropping off tourists on a popular strip in Koh Samui, it was suspected to be linked to the ‘Samui taxi mafia’.

The alleged killer, alongside 11 other suspects, have since been arrested and Sikharin’s family fled the island fearing ‘mafia’ retribution after receiving suspicious calls asking about their whereabouts. Police say the shooting followed a personal dispute.



Now yet another mafia crackdown has since been announced by Thai authorities after they received reports of a series of safety incidents and assaults on foreign tourists at well-known holiday islands.

Officials have also warned any state officials involved, turning a blind eye or facilitating offenders, would face “legal action to the fullest extent”.

One man who knows Thailand’s crooked underworld all too well is Jonathan Wheeler, now 65, and living in Southampton, after spending 18 years in prison for trying to smuggle 4lb of heroin out of the country.

“Thailand’s mafia is not like the Sicilian mafia, they are smaller, family mafia groups and are especially prominent on the islands,” Jonathan, who wrote memoir The Tiger Cage: 18 Years In Thai Prison, tells The Sun.

“They deal in drugs, extortion, protection rackets, prostitution, it’s all there. Some work with the triad groups, like 14k, who are a more organised crime group and move drug shipments and buy and sell women for sex – many of whom are virgins.”



Prior to his incarceration in 1994, Jonathan mingled among dangerous figures while coaching and fighting in Thai boxing competitions and narrowly dodged two assassination attempts from mafia groups.

He says killings are mainly carried out by ‘motorcycle hitmen’, who were “10 a penny” and paid as little as £200 to take someone out.

Their targets were typically rival mafia gang members and drug dealers who had encroached on another group’s turf or had an unpaid debt.

“Some killings are arranged from burner phones in prison and paid for with money or a kilo of crystal meth,” Jonathan says. “If someone owes a debt, they will just shoot them, take over their contacts and begin distribution.”

Nipping around on unrestricted 150CC motorbikes and scooters, meaning they accelerate quicker, Jonathan says they are “much faster than a 2,000CC bike”.



Handguns are the weapon of choice for them, he claims. They ride up, shoot and escape by weaving through traffic at speed and then throw away the weapon.

Jonathan claims that, in Thailand, weapons are “more easily accessible than in America”, with handguns being flogged for £330, M16 assault rifles for £500 and grenades for £11.

Some of the weapons are nicked from military and police armouries to sell on, he alleges.



In the last five years, Thai officers have seized at least 51 assault rifles stolen from their arsenals. And back in May, two M16 rifles, 790 rounds of ammo, grenades, mines and nearly 5kg of explosives were retrieved after being sold to crime groups.

Jonathan narrowly escaped two assassination attempts, once he was nearly rammed off the road for selling hashish on someone else’s patch.

The other happened in Koh Samui after he objected to 22kilos of weed, stashed inside four bin-liners, being stored in a bungalow he was staying at.

“I said, ‘Get the f*** out’, which he did,” he recalls. “He put it in another bungalow. Because I was a witness to it they didn’t want the truth coming out and sent a little guy to come kill me.

“Fortunately, I was sober. It was 3am outside a bar. I saw him walk out of the shadows and pull a revolver out of his jacket.”



He managed to draw attention to the shooter, stopping him in his tracks.

Jonathan describes the Thai mafia gangs as “fearless” because all carry guns, adding: “Even if you’re a champion fighter, they don’t give a f*** because they can just shoot you.”

Some of the killers are especially violent. One mafia member boasted to Jonathan about his bloodthirsty payback after being badly beaten-up by three men.

Jonathan continues: “He caught two of them, grabbing them by the hair and shooting them in the head. It was a brutal revenge.

“He claimed to have paid the police 100,000baht (£2.2k) to make the problem go away. That was the late ’80s, he told me he could help with any problem other than drugs.”



Jonathan also recalls seeing the “No1 mafia boss” of Koh Samui, a man in his 70s, who always had two women in their 40s on his arm and drove around in an old buggy.

Another time, he recalled seeing another mafia man on a motorbike with a cigarette hanging out his mouth, when he hit a police officer “knocking him out”.

“Nothing happened because the mafia guy paid him off,” he says. “To be able to punch a policeman you have to be very powerful.”



Another of the Thai mafia’s trades is sex work. He claims poor families in the north-east are targeted and women go from “picking rice in a field to dancing on a pole and prostitution”.

“Some are happy to loan their daughters for a year in exchange for a motorbike or a scooter, which costs around £800,” Jonathan says.

“Most of these girls have never worn a g-string or a bra in their life before. They are available for sex and often will stay with men for multiple days at a time.”

Jonathan claims that if the sex worker has a brother who is working for the gang, he “will always push her to charge more”.

In addition to those trades, he says many operate extortion and protection rackets and some “higher-ups” rent out bungalows to rich tourists “with everything they want, including drugs”.



Many of the most dangerous aspects, which Thai police have continued to crack down upon, will go unnoticed by tourists – but there are still pitfalls to be wary of.

“For tourists, they just try to rinse them for what they can – whether it’s charging more to reach islands by boat, taxis, tuk-tuks or selling the whole spectrum including drugs,” Jonathan says.

Luke, not his real name, who has spent three years living in Thailand, tells us “there’s a scammer on every corner” waiting to con tourists out of cash.

He says: “It could be fake police, criminals posing as officers, to fine drunken tourists or vendors renting out faulty jet skis that break down leaving you liable to pay for ‘repairs.’”

Another scam he recalled was drivers on taxi apps, like Bolt or Grab, cancelling their job and asking riders to pay in cash – only upon arrival to demand a rate as much as 10 times higher.



Brits who emigrate to Thailand face similar difficulties, according to Rich Mason, 45, from Leicestershire, who claims he was conned out of £100,000 after investing in a business and is now reliant on GoFundMe donations.

He bought shares in gym firm Legacy Muscle Universe Company Limited only for the Thai owners to refuse to pay out dividends, block his phone number and try to get him deported to evade payment.

“The whole thing was just a lie,” Rich tells us. “They even tried to bribe my girlfriend to turn on me and file a fake police report to get me deported to prevent them having to pay me.



“She told me right away. I called them and shouted, ‘What the f*** are you playing at?’ and they hung up. They blocked me on everything soon after.”

He says they claimed to be part of the Thai mafia, threatening him and also pals, telling them: “He die, he die. If I see him, I kill him.”

Rich adds: “He made a lot of threats and tried bully boy and scare tactics, even telling my girlfriend if I came back I’d be in ‘big trouble.’”

His situation worsened when he was near-fatally runover in March, which “smashed my leg to pieces”. He suffered broken feet, pneumonia and blood clots in his lung and leg.

Rich says: “I was left for dead, I died twice and think they were hoping it would be my end so they could take my money. That’s how ruthless they are.



“As a foreigner living in Thailand, you have minimal to zero rights, so you can get scammed and there’s not much you can do about it.

“Don’t invest or build any business unless you have a lot of money, very good legal representation and are 100 per cent sure about it.”

When contacted by The Sun, the owners of Legacy Muscle Universe denied Rich’s claims, insisting he will be paid on the one year anniversary of his investment. Rich argues this wasn’t their agreement and currently, no money has materialised.

In spite of his troubles, Rich, who is still recovering in Thailand and is reliant on donations due to having no financial support, doesn’t dissuade others from visiting.

But he has a strong warning, telling us: “Before everything that happened, I thought of Thailand as this dream paradise that was magical.



“But if you live here, you’re in a very unstable position. You don’t have the same rights as Thai people and that dream of Thailand doesn’t last forever.”

The Sun contacted the Royal Thai Government and Royal Thai Police but did not receive a response. The Tourism Authority of Thailand applauded The Sun for “shedding light on this issue” but was unable to comment further.

News.title: Man in hospital after being ‘attacked and sexually assaulted’ in town centre in the early hours
News.content:
HORROR 'ASSAULT' Man in hospital after being ‘attacked and sexually assaulted’ in town centre in the early hours

A MAN has been rushed to hospital after he was allegedly attacked and sexually assaulted in a town centre in the early hours.

The reported incident unfolded in Macclesfield, Cheshire, at around 1am on Tuesday.

Police were called to the scene on Churchill Way after receiving reports that a man had been assaulted and sexually assaulted.

The victim was taken to hospital in an ambulance where he remains at this time.





Cheshire Constabulary is appealing for anyone with any information that may assist their probe into the horror to come forward.

The force is also asking for anyone with dashcam footage or any witnesses to contact police immediately.

DI Claire Miles said: “An investigation is currently ongoing, and we would like to hear from anyone who may have witnessed the incident or saw anything suspicious or relevant in the area before or after it is believed to have occurred.

“We would also ask anyone who was driving in Macclesfield town centre between 10.40pm on Monday 10 August and 1.10am on Tuesday 11 August, to please check their dashcam footage to see if anything relevant has been captured.



“This includes near to the Churchill Way and Sunderland Street area.

“Anyone with any concerns, or to report any information, should contact Cheshire Police on 101 or report online, quoting IML-2393346.”

News.title: Brit flight to Spain catches stunning moment solar eclipse blackens sky mid-air as pilot warns passengers about looking
News.content:
THIS is the incredible moment travellers on a flight from the UK to Spain caught a stunning solar eclipse in mid-air.

The footage, which was filmed by a passenger on flight BA2644 from Gatwick to Malaga, saw the once-in-a-lifetime celestial event happening while thousands of feet in the air.



Passengers were left in awe as they caught a glimpse of the best solar eclipse in almost three decades.

The video shows how the moon had slowly edged in front of sun, blocking it out in a perfect circle to provide a memory those on the flight would never forget.



Hundreds of lucky passengers on the flight managed to watch the unique moment from a front-row seat above the clouds.

The pilot could be heard warning passengers about exercising caution while looking and not to stare directly.

Passengers could not hold back their excitement as they could be heard murmuring and gasping as they watched the rare phenomenon unfold before their eyes.

In parts of Spain as well as Iceland and Greenland, the sun was completely covered by the moon – known as totality.

And the stunning footage which reflected this phenomenon was captured not far from the Bay of Biscay near northern Spain.

The path of totality was at its strongest in this region, according to astronomers.



Today’s solar eclipse will be the first total solar eclipse visible from the Iberian Peninsula since 1912.

It comes as thousands of Brits back home gathered at viewpoints across the UK, including beaches and parks to witness the incredible celestial event.

Up to 95 per cent of the Sun was obscured by the moon in certain parts of the country as the eclipse peaked.



Brits heeded advice to avoid staring directly at the spectacle with millions turning out wearing sun-safe ­goggles to watch the stellar event.

Others armed themselves with colanders, cardboard contraptions and even welding masks.

In cities, crowds took to parks and rooftops as the eclipse brought traffic to a stop while birds ceased singing.

Witnesses who joined the Bristol Astronomical Society on the Avon Gorge described an eerie feeling as the temperature cooled and the sky went dark.

Sadly, not all parts of the UK got to see a clear view of the eclipse.



Lots of views in Scotland and other parts of the country were blocked by clouds, though much of England enjoyed bright clear skies.

Countryside residents got the most dramatic effect thanks to minimal light pollution.

Parts of northern England missed out because of cloud cover.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And in Belfast, people marvelled at the eclipse as it shone bright through dark clouds.

The next time the sun will be obscured so much in the UK will be 2081.

News.title: Midwife urges parents against 'nappy only' sleep in heatwave - 'it's a mistake'
News.content:
Midwife urges parents against 'nappy only' sleep in heatwave - 'it's a mistake'

A registered midwife has shared a common mistake parents make when it comes to their baby's sleep during a heatwave - and it's something you should avoid

View Image Lily Foggan is a trained midwife

When temperatures soar, it can be tricky to know exactly what to dress your baby in at bedtime to make sure they stay comfortable throughout the night. Getting the balance right is no easy task – too many layers and they could overheat, but too few and they may not be warm enough.

‌



Now, a registered midwife is warning parents to avoid making one common mistake when it comes to their child or baby's sleep during periods of hot weather.

‌



The ideal room temperature for a sleeping baby is between 16–20°C, and organisations such as The Lullaby Trust recommend maintaining the nursery within this range to reduce the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome.

‌



However, as temperatures climb, it can prove difficult to keep bedrooms cool – meaning parents must improvise by removing layers of clothing from their children, reducing the number of blankets or even lowering the tog of a sleeping bag.

Registered midwife Lily Foggan is now warning parents to stop making one mistake when it comes to dressing their children for sleep during a heatwave.

Lily said: "In hot weather, babies obviously need fewer layers than normal. Lightweight sleepwear and lower-tog sleep bags are usually preferable to blankets, which can be kicked off or accidentally cover a baby's face.

‌

"However, a common mistake I see is parents leaving their baby in a nappy overnight, with nothing else, in fear of them getting too hot.

"Remember, usually we're sleeping with a duvet and pyjamas, so they will need something similar."

‌



She added: "Check their chest or the back of their neck for a more accurate indication of temperature, or can also check their temperature.

"The Tommee Tippee No Touch Digital Thermometer is great at eliminating the risk of waking them up, which no one wants, especially during a heatwave."

News.title: A-Level results live: Record number get into Uni or college as pupils check UCAS
News.content:
Hundreds and thousands of students will get their A-Level results today (stock)

UCAS figures show a record number of 18-year-old have been accepted on to degree courses this year, rising by 3% compared to last A-level results day

Students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland are receiving their A-Level, BTec and T-level today.

Most schools and colleges are now open for students to pick up their physical results slips, however students will have already be able to view their university application status via the UCAS portal prior to this.

The total number of 18-year-olds accepted on to degree courses has risen by 3% on the same point last year, with a record high of 262,820 taking up places so far, initial UCAS figures show.

As the results come in and the cost of universities has been in the spotlight. The chief of Universities UK, which represents more than 140 vice-chancellors, urged pupils to not "let politicians make your decision for you".

Last year, the proportion of students getting top A-level results reached a record high, with schools likely facing pressure to continue to produce these outcomes. In 2025 28.3% of all grades across England, Wales and Northern Ireland came in at A* or A.

News.title: Saddleworth Moor fire: Emergency crews battle moorland blaze as road closed
News.content:
The blaze has broken out at Saddleworth Moor in Greater Manchester

Residents have been told to avoid Saddleworth Moor in Greater Manchester as fire crews have been tackling the huge fire which has broken out overnight

Firefighters are tackling a massive blaze in Greater Manchester which has engulfed a huge area of moorland.

In a statement issued on Thursday, a spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service confirmed: "Our crews have been tackling a moorland fire near Holmfirth Road in Oldham through the night. Please avoid the area while emergency services respond to the incident."

The blaze at Saddleworth Moor comes after wildfires have ravaged Greater Manchester and sections of the UK over the summer. Major blazes erupted at Dovestone and Tintwistle earlier this summer, with the fires damaging nearly 1,000 acres of land.

News.title: Cold case cops hunt hitman hired by cheating husband to bludgeon wife to death
News.content:
Cold case cops hunt hitman hired by cheating husband to bludgeon wife to death

EXCLUSIVE: Detectives have urged anyone with information to come forward as they continue to search for a contract killer hired by cheating Allen Morgan to hack his wife, Carol, to death in 1981

View 6 Images Allen Morgan and his second wife Margaret went on trial at Luton Crown Court where she was acquitted of conspiracy to murder (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Cold case detectives are hunting a hitman hired by a cheating husband to bludgeon his wife to death - exactly 45 years after the brutal murder.

‌



Allen Morgan enlisted a contract killer to hack his wife, Carol, 36, to death at the convenience store they owned so he could start a new life with his lover. The killer, who has never been caught, used an axe or machete to rain up to 15 blows on her body and skull.

‌



He then fled with cash and cigarettes following the attack in August 1981. The Mirror understands Morgan - who was handed a life sentence in 2024 - is planning to appeal against his conviction. But police say they are still desperate to give "answers" to Carol's family.

‌



View 6 Images Carol Morgan was found hacked to death at the convenience store she ran with her husband in Bedfordshire on August 13 1981 (Image: PA)

Cheating husband who hired hitman to bash his wife to death launches appeal bid READ MORE :

How 'twisted' cheating husband who plotted to kill wife hid in plain sight in bold TV interviews READ MORE :

In a statement released to mark the anniversary of Carol's murder, Det Chief Insp Richard Stott from Bedfordshire Police said: “No murder investigation is ever closed, and the case of Carol Morgan’s murder remains under review by cold case detectives for any potential further lines of enquiry.

"Carol was brutally killed 45 years ago and sadly her family are still left without some answers as to what happened to her. We would always encourage anyone who knew Carol or who has any information at all about her death to come forward, as any information – no matter how small – could aid our investigation.”

‌



Carol was found murdered at the convenience store she ran with her husband, then aged 31, in Linslade, Bedfordshire, on August 13 1981. At the time of the victim’s death, there was not enough evidence to charge anyone in connection with the case and her husband was not considered a suspect, the Crown Prosecution Service said.

View 6 Images After Carol's murder, Morgan spoke to journalists to deny any involvement in his wife's murder (Image: PA)

The case was reopened by detectives in 2018 following a review by a cold case team. Morgan was tried alongside his current wife, teacher Margaret Morgan, then 75, who was also charged with conspiracy to murder but was acquitted by a jury, police said.

‌



Morgan's conspiracy to murder trial in 2023 was told he found Carol's body in the storeroom of Morgan’s Food Fare when he returned from the cinema in Luton, 14 miles away, with her two children Dean, 14, and Jane, 12. The prosecution at Luton Crown Court said the trip gave Morgan a “cast-iron” alibi and allowed a paid hitman to murder and rob Carol.

Morgan, who walks with a stick, from Stanstead Crescent, Woodingdean, Brighton, was sentenced to life for conspiracy to murder by Justice Martin Spencer who told him: “In reality you will be spending the rest of your life in prison.”

View 6 Images Morgan was jailed for life with a minimum term of 22 years for plotting to kill his then-wife and told he would likely die in jail

‌



At the time of the killing, detectives believed Carol had been the victim of a burglary gone wrong. The cold case investigation uncovered a star witness who revealed that Morgan had wanted to find a hitman to kill Carol.

Jane Bunting, 62, met the couple in the Dolphin pub in Linslade in the weeks before the murder. She told the jury she was aged 17 and was “appalled” and “horrified” when Morgan asked if her ex-boyfriend knew anyone who could kill.

She said: “He'd say, 'I hate Carol', 'I don't want to be married to her', 'I wish she'd die', 'Wouldn’t an accident be nice?'" She told the jury Morgan said: “'You can always pay someone'.

‌



View 6 Images Carol suffered 15 blows to the body when she was murdered in the basement of her shop, Morgan’s Food Fare (Image: Bedfordshire Police )

"He turned to me directly and addressed me and said, 'What about that Danny Mayhew you went out with? He's a bit of a criminal, wouldn't he know someone?'" She said she got up and left. Carol and Morgan met at a single parents’ group in Swindon called Gingerbread. They married in March 1977 and moved to the shop in December 1979.

About a year before the murder, Morgan and mother-of-two Margaret Spooner, as she was then known, began an affair. Morgan visited Margaret at her home while her husband Michael was at work. Once a neighbour walked in as Margaret came down the stairs with no tights on, followed by Morgan.

‌



Margaret said Morgan had been trying on a Father Christmas outfit for the playgroup party. Carol’s first husband Richard Curtis, now 78, said the money to buy the shop came from Carol’s share of their matrimonial home in Covingham, Swindon. He paid maintenance for the children.

View 6 Images Following Carol's murder, police issued an appeal to trace a man seen outside her shop with a bag of cash (Image: PA)

By 1981 Morgan and Carol were living hand to mouth and had spiralling debts. She had made a will leaving her entire estate to Morgan. The shop had been purchased on an unsecured £6,000 loan that had a life insurance policy linked to it.

‌



Prosecutor Pavlos Panayi KC told the 2023 trial: “The two defendants wanted to be together, but could not be together while Allen remained married to Carol Morgan. He could not divorce his wife. These two individuals were involved in a passionate, but forbidden and adulterous love affair.”

Carol, who had closed the shop at 6pm, was battered with an axe or machete. There was no sign of a break in at the shop and the family’s Labrador-Collie, that normally had the run of the premises, had been shut in one of the bedrooms in the flat above the shop.

Mr Panayi said: “Blow after blow rained down on her causing the most awful of injuries The killer was determined to make sure the victim was dead before he left the premises - that is what the defendant paid him to do.”

Article continues below

Around £400 cash was taken from a desk that had “a secret mechanism”. It would not open unless another, middle drawer, was moved into an exact position. £35 was also snatched from the till, along with 1,400 cigarettes.

The prosecutor said: “The killer had some inside information before entering the premises. The obvious conclusion was that the killer was told by Allen Morgan where he would find the cash which may well have constituted part-payment for the murder.”

Unexplained cash withdrawals had been made in the days leading up to the murder. On the day of the killing Morgan had told the police he was asleep when he was seen at a branch of Nationwide withdrawing £250.

News.title: Pharmacist issues new warning for anyone taking Mounjaro or Wegovy
News.content:
Pharmacist issues new warning for anyone taking Mounjaro or Wegovy

There is a list of symptoms to watch out for as alerts come into force this week

View 3 Images Millions are taking the weight-loss jabs

A pharmacist has issued a warning to Wegovy and Mounjaro users as the nation braces for its fifth heatwave of 2026. The warning comes as more than half of England and the whole of Wales are in drought, with some 20 million Brits living under water restrictions.

‌



Amber warnings of extreme heat health risks are in force with the Met Office saying Thursday could be the hottest ever August day on record at over 38C. Temperatures are forecast to peak on Thursday.

‌



Wendy Lee, Deputy Superintendent at Well Pharmacy said: “The heat increases the risk of fluid loss through sweating, which can in turn lead to dehydration. Weight-loss medications like Wegovy, and Mounjaro can suppress appetite, reduce the urge to eat and drink regularly and cause nausea or vomiting, so it’s very easy to become dehydrated.”

‌



View 3 Images Heatwave warnings have been issued

Around 1.6 to 1.9 million UK adults currently use or have recently used these weight-loss medications. Wendy said: “Around one in every 30 to 35 adults in Britain are currently taking weight-loss medication - this is a lot of people at risk of becoming seriously ill if they fail to stay hydrated.

Most users obtain the drugs privately rather than through the NHS, with Mounjaro now the most commonly used weight-loss injection for weight loss treatment. Wendy explained the early warning signs of dehydration before it is too late:

‌



Wendy said: “Look out for thirst, a dry mouth or sticky saliva. Headaches are often common with dehydration, as is dark yellow urine, or low levels of urination altogether. And if you are feeling tired or weak, or dizzy when you get up, this could be another indicator that you are becoming dehydrated.”

“But if you feel confused or unusually drowsy, faint or have a rapid heartbeat or have very little or no urine, this is serious and you should seek urgent medical attention. Similarly, if you are unable to keep fluids down because of vomiting or you feel extremely weak, these are all signs of severe dehydration.

View 3 Images You need to keep drinking

‌



“Typical heatstroke symptoms can include body temperature exceeding 40 degrees, hot skin, confusion, fainting or losing consciousness.”

Advising all those using weight loss medication to be particularly vigilant in the extreme heat, Wendy has tips for heat hydration.

She said: “In hot weather, most adults should aim to drink 2.5 to 3 litres of water daily to replenish fluids lost through sweating. This is an increase from the baseline recommendation of 1.5 to 2 litres. Remember to pace yourself and sip water steadily rather than drinking massive amounts all at once. If you are exercising or working in the heat, aim for roughly 1 cup (240 ml) every 15 to 20 minutes.

Article continues below

“And, avoid overhydration: Do not exceed 1.5 litres per hour, as this can dangerously lower your blood salt levels.”

News.title: What are severe acid reflux symptoms - condition affects 20 percent of UK adults
News.content:
What are severe acid reflux symptoms - condition affects 20 percent of UK adults

Severe acid reflux affects 20 per cent of UK adults - but what are the symptoms of the condition, what causes it, and how can you treat it?

View 3 Images Acid reflux affects large numbers of UK adults - but what are the symptoms and how can you treat it? (Image: Giselleflissak via Getty Images)

Severe acid reflux is a condition that affects far more people than you might think. According to Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, 20 per cent of UK adults suffer from severe acid reflux - commonly experienced as heartburn, a burning sensation in the centre of the chest.

‌



For some sufferers, this triggers severe pain, regurgitation, difficulty swallowing, coughing, asthma, insomnia, voice loss, teeth and gum damage, nutritional problems and depression. Heartburn is a burning feeling in the chest caused by stomach acid travelling up towards the throat (acid reflux). If it persists, it may be diagnosed as gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD).

‌



Many people experience heartburn occasionally, often with no obvious cause. The NHS website states it is sometimes triggered or worsened by certain food and drink – such as coffee, tomatoes, alcohol, chocolate and fatty or spicy foods - as well as by being overweight or smoking.

‌



It can also be brought on by pregnancy, stress and anxiety, or a rise in certain hormones, such as progesterone and oestrogen. Additional causes can include certain medications, such as anti-inflammatory painkillers (like ibuprofen), a hiatus hernia – where part of your stomach moves up into your chest - a stomach ulcer, or a bacterial infection in your stomach.

How can acid reflux be treated and w hat are the tell-tale signs?

If you are diagnosed with acid reflux, a GP may prescribe medication known as a proton pump inhibitor (PPI), which reduces the amount of acid your stomach produces. Well-known PPIs include omeprazole and lansoprazole.

You'll typically need to take this type of medication for four or eight weeks, depending on the severity of your acid reflux. Return to your GP if your symptoms come back after stopping your medication. You may require a long-term prescription.

‌



Dr Amir Khan, a prominent TV GP frequently seen on GMB and Lorraine, cautioned users of such medication this week. He said: "Brilliant medication for acid reflux and protecting the stomach, but if you're taking them for months or years, they can reduce absorption of nutrients like vitamin B12 and magnesium. So they should be reviewed from time to time. Make sure you still need them and that you're on the lowest possible dose to manage your symptoms."

View 3 Images You can get help to ease acid reflux but you must see a medical professional (Image: bymuratdeniz via Getty Images)

Lansoprazole and omeprazole are proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) that reduce the amount of acid your stomach produces. They treat acid reflux, GERD, stomach and duodenal ulcers, erosive oesophagitis, and hypersecretory conditions like Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

‌



They are also combined with antibiotics to eliminate H. pylori bacterial infections and prevent ulcers caused by NSAID painkillers. The NHS states the symptoms of acid reflux are: heartburn or an unpleasant sour taste in your mouth, caused by stomach acid.

It notes you may also experience bad breath, bloating and feeling sick, a cough or hiccups that keep returning, or a hoarse voice. Symptoms are often worse after eating, when lying down and when bending over.

Three ways to tackle acid reflux - NHS advice

The NHS recommends three main ways to treat it. There are three lifestyle adjustments that can help ease symptoms: eating smaller, more frequent meals; attempting to lose weight if you are overweight; and finding ways to de-stress.

‌



The NHS also highlights six things to steer clear of. Firstly, avoid food or drink that triggers your symptoms. Secondly, do not eat within 3 or 4 hours before bed. Thirdly, avoid wearing clothing that is tight around your waist.

Fourthly, do not smoke. Fifthly, avoid drinking too much alcohol. Finally, never stop taking any prescribed medication without consulting a doctor first.

View 3 Images Acid reflux can be unpleasant and hard to get rid of (Image: Drazen_ via Getty Images)

‌



If heartburn persists, seek advice from a pharmacist, who may suggest antacids or alginates to help relieve your symptoms. These are best taken with food or shortly after eating, as this is when heartburn is most likely to strike, and may also prove more effective when taken alongside a meal.

While antacids and alginates offer short-term relief, they are not a long-term solution and should not be taken regularly over extended periods. If you are pregnant, a pharmacist can advise on suitable medicines. However, you should visit your GP if lifestyle changes and over-the-counter remedies are failing to tackle your heartburn; if you suffer from heartburn most days; or if you experience additional symptoms such as food becoming lodged in your throat, frequent vomiting, or unexplained weight loss.

The NHS website says: "A GP can provide alternative or stronger treatments and help rule out any more serious causes of your symptoms. If at any time you feel your symptoms are getting worse, contact a GP, go to 111.nhs.uk or call 111." What if this still does not work?

Article continues below

If medicines fail to provide relief or your symptoms are particularly severe, a GP may refer you to a specialist for:

News.title: 'I go to the gym and eat salads but still ended up a size 30'
News.content:
'I go to the gym and eat salads but still ended up a size 30'

Abigail Barry says doctors just told her to 'put some effort in' and lose weight until she got her diagnosis

View 8 Images Abigail Barry wants to raise awareness

A mum says she spent years being told to "eat less and exercise more" before finally discovering she was living with a chronic illness that causes her legs to dramatically swell. Abigail Barry says doctors repeatedly blamed her weight – despite her desperately following healthy diets, exercising regularly and maintaining an active lifestyle.

‌



The 52-year-old was finally diagnosed this year with advanced lymphoedema and lipoedema. Despite her healthy lifestyle, the condition means she gets a build-up of lymph fluid in her legs, causing them to painfully swell, and leading to weight gain and struggles to walk.

‌



Abigail is now spending £300 a month on weight loss jabs in a desperate attempt to reclaim her life, having been left housebound by the condition. “It was absolutely soul-destroying to be told I wasn’t trying hard enough when I was doing everything right,' said Abigail, a former motorcycle instructor from Herne Bay, Kent. “It often got me really down and depressed.

‌



View 8 Images Abigail before her weight gain

“I'd be dog walking, going to the gym and still putting on weight. I took either my mum or ex-partner to consultations to back me up that I wasn't overeating, but that was just ignored.

“I then became incredibly angry at consultants as they just wouldn't help and kept referring me to dietitians.”

‌



The mum-of-two first noticed she was gaining weight at 18 years old, and she struggled to lose weight even when following a low-fat, high-fibre diet. She said: “I would also get bruises very, very easily, and my rings would get very tight overnight. Doctors have been telling me for years to lose weight, eat less, exercise, and it's my fault that I'm the size I am, as I must be eating more than I should.

“I was told to put some real effort in. I was lost for words, because at that time, I was doing Weight Watchers, at the gym five times, water aerobics, bikes, weights, walking my dog twice a day and eating a healthy diet.

View 8 Images Abigail took years to get a diagnosis

‌



'I was eating healthily: black coffee, two scrambled eggs on one slice of brown toast with a scraping of Marmite, and a banana for breakfast Lunch was shredded chicken or turkey breast with lettuce, cucumber, and a mashed avocado inside a whole-wheat tortilla, with an apple and strawberries.

“Dinner was usually turkey breast, a hard-boiled egg, and a low-calorie dressing over a bed of mixed greens salad and spring onion. I snack on cheese and onion rice cakes, plain popcorn, hummus and carrot sticks, air-fried broccoli, pre-portioned nuts and protein bars.

“I don’t overeat – but not once have they told me it's because of my illnesses that I'm obese. GPs and consultants have always told me to try harder.”

‌



View 8 Images Abigail says doctors missed the real cause of her weight gain

Abigail was finally diagnosed after she was admitted to hospital for fistula surgery and a consultant recognised the signs. Lymphoedema is a long-term condition that causes swelling in the body's tissues. It can affect any part of the body, but usually develops in the arms or legs.

Four months ago, Abigail began paying more than £300 a month for private weight-loss injections, which she says have reduced pain and swelling. Abigail said: “Because I’m not diabetic, I have to pay, and I'm absolutely, 100% sure that I'm only fat because of my illnesses.

‌



“I'm disgusted that I have to pay. The money spent on jabs could be put towards compression stockings and velcro wraps, antidepressants, and counselling services. Within the first two weeks, the pain and a lot of the swelling went down in my legs.

View 8 Images Abigail's legs and feet swell and bruise

“During the second month, I had extreme nausea and vomiting, and my stomach felt constantly heavy and uncomfortable, like I was nine months pregnant. Then it calmed down, but in the third month, I had the nausea, vomiting and an uncomfortable stomach for about four days.

‌



“I’m extremely tired, irritable and grumpy, which is unlike me.”

Now housebound and unable to work, Abigail is a size 30, uses a vibration plate to help with pain and wears compression socks daily. Abigail said: “If I don’t wear my compression garments, my legs balloon in size. I'm finding it very difficult to actually compress my legs daily as it's difficult to reach due to my obesity.

“It’s very time-consuming. It takes a lot of time and strength to wrap my legs, then I have to keep my legs moisturised and in good condition.

‌



View 8 Images Abigail started gaining weight in her teens

“I also have to elevate my legs daily. I do this by lying on the bed and putting both my legs above my head, resting on a wall, and I have to keep them there for 40 minutes twice a day to help drain the lymph fluid. I’ve often been caught doing this by my window cleaner – the poor fella.

“It's very hard to do most things due to the heaviness, pain and size of my legs. I can’t walk as my legs are so painful and heavy. I can’t stand for any period or do things that involve standing.

‌



“I’m unbelievably stubborn and hate using a wheelchair or scooter. When I make myself do my housework, it’s physically painful. It’s a vicious cycle.”

View 8 Images Abigail struggles with everyday life

Abigail says strangers have thrown abuse at her for using disabled parking bays and she’s often stared at due to her size. She said: “To start with, I was incredibly embarrassed by my size and my legs, but since finding out it's actually a medical problem, I have become very forgiving of myself with a devil-may-care attitude.

‌



“I wear short shorts and smile at everyone. I've had people shout at me to stop using disabled bays, people telling me to eat less, do more exercise and tell me I'm not healthy.

“If anyone stares now, I just give them a massive smile, and so far they have always smiled back.” Abigail is sharing her story to raise awareness of her condition. She has begun sharing photographs and videos of her condition on her TikTok account @‌abigailbarry_the1andonly and says many women have since contacted her after recognising the symptoms in themselves.

View 8 Images Abigail says she shouldn't have to pay

Article continues below

Abigail added: “If you have lymphoedema, don't give up. Early detection and treatment would be life-changing. Lymphoedema and lipoedema are highly manageable conditions if you get yourself a good specialist and treat from the outset.

“It's not curable, but it is liveable; you can control the swelling and pain if you get a good routine going. Don’t be embarrassed.”

News.title: Once loved UK theme park left 'eerily' derelict for over a decade after closing forever
News.content:
Once loved UK theme park left 'eerily' derelict for over a decade after closing forever

Pleasure Island shut its gates for the last time in 2016 and now the once loved tourist attraction sits eerily derelict with some of its original structures remaining - as future plans remain unclear

View 4 Images Inside Pleasure Island, Cleethorpes before demolition begins

A once loved UK theme park has now been sitting derelict for over 10 years, as plans to develop the former tourist attraction continue to face pushbacks.

‌



The Lincolnshire seaside resort, Cleethorpes, was home to Pleasure Island Family Theme Park from May 1993 until 2016.

‌



Every year, tens of thousands of visitors made their way to the amusement park before its sudden closure.

‌



View 4 Images The theme park has been closed for over a decade

The huge location featured nearly 50 rides, many of which had legendary status among thrill-seekers, including the Hyperblaster, Obliterator, Pendulus, and Terror Rack.

However, the appeal began to drop in the mid-2000s as Brits began replacing stay at home holidays for trips abroad due to costs. Pleasure Island's footfall rapidly declined, and in 2016 the gates shut forever at the end of the season.

‌



Following its closure, several rides were sold at auction, including the historic 1904 carousel, with most other rides demolished in 2018.

However, despite shutting over a decade ago, the site remains entirely derelict with a distinctly eery feel.

Structures still stand, including the dodgems building and children's entertainment zone, as much of the park sits in disrepair.

‌



View 4 Images Pleasure Island Development Site in Cleethorpes

The entrance stands somewhat similar to how it did all those years ago, however metal fencing encloses the derelict site covering the 'welcome' sign.

As the land appears to have stood still, nature appears to have taken over, with plants and weeds growing across all areas. However, plans to reinvent the space have been proposed.

‌



These plans involve the construction of two hotels, hundreds of log cabins, a casino and additional leisure facilities.

View 4 Images Inside Pleasure Island, Cleethorpes before demolition begins

They first emerged in 2022 and are estimated to require around £65 million in investment. The ambitious, wide-ranging plans reportedly include restaurants, cafés and retail outlets, while also making use of the lake for fishing.

‌



But, since they were announced, the plans have faced considerable pushback from a number of organisations, and whether they will ultimately go ahead remains unclear.

The Environment Agency was the first to voice concerns, highlighting issues surrounding flooding.

The body released a statement, saying: "We will require continuous access along both banks of the watercourse, and as a minimum, the bridge should not reduce the cross-sectional area of the channel. Further details are required to determine whether these requirements have been met."

Article continues below

Natural England has also warned that the development could pose a threat to the wellbeing of the neighbouring Humber Estuary.

News.title: Once-in-a-generation solar eclipse wows millions in UK and Europe
News.content:
The UK and Europe have enjoyed their most dramatic solar eclipse for nearly 30 years, with millions thought to have witnessed the once-in-a-generation event.

Those watching the astronomical phenomenon from the UK were treated to a partial eclipse, which peaked shortly after 19:00 BST, when most saw more than 90% of the Sun covered by the Moon.

But parts of Greenland, Iceland and Spain experienced the complete darkness and spectacle of a total eclipse.

Large crowds at viewing sites across the UK and Europe reacted with gasps and cheers, with astronomy enthusiasts saying it served as a reminder of how "amazing" the Universe is.

News.title: Watch: Moment 'surreal' solar eclipse witnessed in UK and Europe
News.content:
Millions of people across Europe and the UK witnessed the most significant solar eclipse since 1999 on Wednesday.

For the UK, more than 90% of the Sun was covered by the Moon, whereas in some parts of Europe, a rare total eclipse could be seen.

BBC science correspondent Pallab Ghosh was in Burgos, Spain, and said he got goosebumps from the spectacle.

News.title: Polls open in Clacton by-election
News.content:
The polls have opened in Clacton-on-Sea as a record number of candidates vie to become the town's next MP.

An electorate of 79,785 registered voters have the chance to vote for one of 34 candidates standing in the Essex resort - the most ever to stand in a British election.

Fifty-one polling stations have opened, covering Clacton and the surrounding towns of Jaywick, Frinton and Walton-on-the-Naze. The constituency also has rural villages including St Osyth, Weeley and Great Bentley.

Voters will need to show a form of acceptable ID - such as a driving licence or passport - to be able to cast their ballot.

They will receive the longest ballot paper in British electoral history at 90cm - about 3ft long - to choose their candidate and cast their vote.

There are 12 political parties and 20 independents standing.

Polling stations will remain open to anyone registered to vote until 22:00, with the count taking place overnight.

News.title: Trump says White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave post
News.content:
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will step down from her position at the end of the month, President Donald Trump has announced.

Leavitt, whom the president called one of his "most trusted aides", will depart from her role to spend time with her young children and family - "a decision I totally understand and respect", Trump wrote in a social media post.

"Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party," he added.

Leavitt, 28, took the job as White House Press Secretary last year - becoming the youngest person to ever have the role. It was not immediately clear who will replace her.

News.title: ICE plans to equip agents with gloves that can deliver electric shocks
News.content:
Unlike a taser, which uses sharp barbs in the skin to deliver a shock of up to 50,000 volts, the gloves do not complete an electrical circuit inside the body.

The gloves instead deliver a sharp shock to convince a subject to comply using "pain deterrence", says Lt Butch Gallion, an administrator at Hawkins County jail in Tennessee.

"We may or may not deploy them. It just depends on how they act. When you push the button to turn them on there's a light that displays. The inmates understand that light, and often just seeing the light brings compliance," he says.

The shocks can only be delivered when they contact skin, allowing an officer to touch a subject's clothing, and then move to the skin â typically the wrist or elbow - if they begin to fight.

If they become combative, he continues, "then you can apply the gloves to an area that the skin is exposed. And it's an instant complier for me".

According to the DHS note, GLOVE would be used by officers and agents in Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), which targets transnational criminal organisations, and Enforcement Removal Operations (ERO), which is responsible for arresting, detaining and deporting people who violate immigration laws in the US.

Some law enforcement agencies are already using the gloves but it's believed that the planned ICE purchase would be the largest from Compliant Technologies to date.

Civil rights groups, including the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), have expressed alarm about law enforcement using them.

"ICE spent the last year showing this country that they are willing to disregard the law and are too quick to use force, with devastating and at times fatal consequences for citizens and noncitizens alike," said Jenn Rolnick Borchetta, deputy director on policing at the ACLU.

Federal immigration agents have been criticised in the wake of fatalities that have occurred during enforcement operations.

Recent incidents include the fatal shooting of Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas, while Colombian national Johan SebastiÃ¡n DurÃ¡n Guerrero was killed during an immigration enforcement operation in Maine.

ICE has also been under pressure to deliver President Donald Trump's deportation agenda, which includes meeting a daily target of arrests.

"Now they [ICE] might be equipped with a device that allows them to deliver an electric shock with their hands by pushing a small button, in a move that might be imperceptible to those watching," Borchetta said.

"Giving immigration agents a concealed means of delivering terrible pain is a recipe for more harm to the public and less accountability."

With reporting by Max Matza

News.title: First 100% British chocolate bar made since 1932
News.content:
A chocolate bar has been made using entirely British ingredients for the first time in nearly a century, with cocoa from not Brazil or Bali, but Berkshire.

Created at the University of Reading, it was named the Reading 100 Chocolate Bar to mark the university's 100th anniversary.

It is the first of its kind since 1932, when Rowntree's gifted a six-year-old Princess Elizabeth the only other bar of UK-grown chocolate ever made.

Food security master's student Maha Khan created the chocolate bar by harvesting, fermenting and processing the Reading-grown cocoa.

While the UK's chocolate market is worth Â£10.4bn, it is entirely reliant on imported cocoa.

Maha told the Today programme she made the bar to highlight the challenges facing the cocoa growing industry.

She said: "It is incredible that we can make 100% British chocolate â but in the context of climate change, pests and diseases, there are estimates that 30 to 40% is lost.

"And we've seen with these heatwaves, climate change, these problems and challenges are only going to get exacerbated."

News.title: Results, appeals and resits - what to do if things don't go to plan
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of A-level students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland are waiting for their results.

They will be released at 08:00 BST on Thursday 13 August.

Those who have applied to university should be able to see whether they have been successful then too, as the Ucas Hub updates at the same time.

Here is everything you need to know about results, appeals and resits.

News.title: How to get the most out of clearing
News.content:
Have you changed your mind about the university course you want to start after getting your results?

Maybe you did not apply to university originally but now want to go, or you might not end up getting the grades you need to make it into your firm choice.

If that is you, the clearing process will have you covered.

While students in Scotland received their results last week, young people in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will find out how they did in their exams on Thursday 13 August.

Here is everything you need to know about clearing.

News.title: Leading doctor rebukes NHS chiefs over transplant failings
News.content:
While NHS Blood and Transplant manages organ donations and supports transplant centres, services are commissioned and paid for by NHS England.

But in a letter to NHS England and a small group of patient advocates, Manas said the central body had created a "fragmented" system "with poor accountability".

There is a "mismatch", he said, between each hospital's waiting lists, organ availability, capacity to carry out surgeries and the availability of operating theatres.

This is "leading to last-minute cancellations [and] unpredictable utilisation of donated organs," he warned.

The BBC reported in March that the UK, once a world leader, had fallen behind major Western nations in heart and lung transplantation, though it fares better in other areas such as kidney transplantation.

The NHS transplants one in 10 lungs and one in seven hearts that are donated - half the proportions seen in some other countries.

It has not invested in modern technology at the same rate as other countries, and suffers from a lack of theatre space, intensive care beds and staff.

Wales and Northern Ireland do not have a heart and lung transplant centre, so patients commonly travel to England for surgery. There is one heart transplant centre in Scotland.

News.title: Scottish Labour leader hopefuls warn against party divisions
News.content:
Scottish Labour leadership contenders have warned about the dangers of internal feuds and briefings at their first party hustings in Glasgow.

Monica Lennon, Joe Fagan and Michael Marra made their cases to succeed Anas Sarwar as they pitched to rebuild Scottish Labour after May's crushing electoral defeat.

Those attending the hour-long event were met by a handful of pro-Palestine protesters, whose shouts were heard during the first part of the event.

All three candidates promised to change, rebuild and unite the party following its worst Holyrood election defeat since devolution.

News.title: GB's Hudson-Smith wins historic 400m gold on home track
News.content:
On his childhood track, in front of a stand named in his honour, hometown hero Matthew Hudson-Smith was not going to be denied.

A full-circle moment, completed by writing his name in history.

More than two decades after stepping foot inside Alexander Stadium for the first time aged nine, Hudson-Smith delivered Great Britain's latest gold in Birmingham to become the joint-most decorated man of all-time at European Championships.

The 31-year-old celebrated the third European 400m title of his illustrious career by making his way into the crowd and placing a hand on the banner bearing his name.

Moments before, Hudson-Smith had stormed down the home straight, just as he had countless times before as a member of local club Birchfield Harriers.

This time, though, the Olympic and world silver medallist did so to rapturous cheers inside the arena which fostered his love for the sport.

With his eighth podium at the championships, Hudson-Smith equalled French sprinter Christophe Lemaitre's men's record medal tally - with the relays still to come.

"Honestly, words can't describe how much that meant to me," he told BBC Sport.

"Nobody was going to beat me on this track. This is my home. I know this track like the back of my hand. I have my stand. Now I'm going to go for Mayor of Birmingham and Wolverhampton!

"I knew I was the best in the world. I knew that, on paper, I was a second faster than every single one of these guys. It was about me and the clock."

News.title: New Forest wildfire continues as temperatures rise
News.content:
Firefighters on the fourth day of battling a wildfire in the New Forest are facing "challenging" weather conditions with temperatures set to rise again

The blaze began on Sunday 9 August when a van caught fire on the A31, with 23 drivers abandoning their vehicles as the fire took hold.

Hampshire & Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service (HIWFRS) said crews had implemented fire breaks and had a 'good hold' of the perimeter of the fire, while changing wind conditions were proving challenging.

National Highways said repairs to the A31 were not expected to be begin until Friday 14 August at the earliest.

News.title: Green councillor charged with assaults
News.content:
A Birmingham Green Party city councillor has been charged with attacking a member of the public, three police officers and a member of police staff.

Siobhan Harper-Nunes, 66, was arrested on suspicion of assault after police were called to the junction of Monument Road and Hagley Road in the city, at about 17:00 BST on 6 August.

Harper-Nunes, of Monument Road, was charged the following day.

West Midlands Police said that she was arrested again at Monument Road on Wednesday morning on suspicion of harassment.

She remained in custody while inquiries continued, police said.

Harper-Nunes will appear at Birmingham Magistrates' Court on 10 September on the assault charges, the force said.

The councillor was elected in May to represent the Ladywood ward for the city council.

She previously stood as the Green Party's candidate for West Midlands mayor in the 2024 election.

The Birmingham Green Party has been approached for comment.

News.title: Victim of fatal Clapham shooting named
News.content:
A man who was shot dead in south-west London has been named by police as Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa.

Officers and paramedics were called to Willington Road, Clapham, just before 22:00 BST on Monday following reports of gunshots near The Landor pub.

The 25-year-old, who worked as a bus driver, was pronounced dead at the scene, the Metropolitan Police said.

A 22-year-old man was later arrested on suspicion of murder after attending hospital with a gunshot wound on Tuesday. He remains in hospital under police guard.

Det Ch Insp Claire Guiver said her thoughts were with the victim's family as they "come to terms with this tragic incident".

News.title: Why is Amanda Knox's upcoming Edinburgh Fringe comedy show causing controversy?
News.content:
Amanda Knox, a woman involved in one of the world's most famous murder cases, is set to perform a comedy show at The Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

Knox was convicted and later acquitted of murdering her British roommate, Meredith Kercher, in Italy in 2007.

Knox's show, Cartwheel, is about motherhood and how she will explain her experiences to her daughter, according to the festival's website.

"I don't joke about Meredith's death. I joke a lot about how I was vilified, but I don't joke about her murder," she had told the Telegraph newspaper, external.

Kercher's sister, Stephanie told BBC Breakfast her sibling "wouldn't find these topics of any comedy value".

A petition against the show, set up by a friend of Meredith, has been signed by just over 2,400 people, and says the show disrespects her memory and also risks normalising violence against women.

A spokesperson for Knox said the show, set to run over 11 days from Friday, honours Kercher's memory.

Find out more about what Stephanie Kercher told the BBC.

News.title: Robbers who pretended to be from Liverpool jailed
News.content:
Two armed robbers who police said pretended to be from Liverpool while they raided a shop have been jailed.

Stephen Bradley and David Oakley threatened staff at Maddy's Store in Church Road, New Mills, Derbyshire, with a knife and imitation firearm.

The pair, who were heard on CCTV saying they needed to "get back to Liverpool", stole Â£4,000 of cigarettes, Â£200 cash and nine bottles of whiskey.

Bradley, 56, and Oakley, 48, were in fact living about "five minutes down the road" from the shop, Derbyshire Police said.

Bradley, of New Street, New Mills, pleaded guilty to robbery and possession of an imitation firearm.

Oakley, of no fixed address, admitted robbery and possession of a knife.

Both were sentenced to four years in prison at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court on 24 June.

The number of school leavers in the UK accepted on to degree courses has risen to a record high this year.

A total of 262,820 UK 18-year-olds have gained a place at university or college – up 3% on the same point last year, according to data published by the university admissions service.

Ucas said it is the highest number of placed students on results day on record, driven by a rising number of 18-year-olds in the population.

The overall number of students, of all ages and domiciles, being accepted has also reached a record high – with 446,690 successful applicants up from 439,180 last year.

Hundreds of thousands of students across England, Wales and Northern Ireland are receiving grades to help them decide whether to progress to university, an apprenticeship or work.

Results day comes amid a crisis in the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet).

open image in gallery Students celebrate A-level, BTEC and T-level results at Oaklands College, 13th Aug 2026 ( Oaklands College )

The Department for Education estimates that nearly 58,000 18-year-olds in England will get no results on Thursday because they have dropped out of education and training, although some are working.

The latest data, published in May, showed the number of young people aged 16 to 24 neither working nor learning surpassed one million for the first time since 2013, reaching 1.01 million in the three months from January to March.

The Education Secretary said she is focused on a “revolution” in technical and vocational pathways to answer the “clarion call” of the Neets crisis.

In a statement ahead of results day, Lucy Powell said: “My priority is making sure every young person has the skills, knowledge, and confidence to thrive in the jobs of the future.

“That’s why we’re giving technical education the respect it deserves by rolling out new V Levels to go alongside A Levels, introducing brilliant routes into the careers of the future from age 14, and fully funding apprenticeship training for under-25s.”

For many students, receiving their exam results on Thursday will also bring confirmation of university places.

On the day before A-level results day, a sample of 131 of the UK’s largest higher education providers showed there were 22,698 courses with vacancies for undergraduate students living in England on the Ucas clearing site – which matches applicants to university places yet to be filled.

Eighteen of the 24 Russell Group universities, which represent some of the most selective UK institutions, had vacancies on courses for English residents – a total of 3,483 courses between them.
