Donald Trump is being sued over a new plan to charge as much as $100,000 for early access to his social posts.

The lawsuit is an attempt to stop him profiting from a new service on his own Truth Social platform, which gives subscribers early, exclusive access to his posts about US policy.

It contends that Trump’s agreement to publish updates concerning tariffs, war and government actions first on his platform violates the Constitution, asserting that public announcements should be distributed to everyone concurrently.

This action follows a subscription product launched earlier this month by Trump Media & Technology, charging Wall Street firms as much as $100,000 a month for faster access to trade on the information.

"A president selling priority access to news he himself generates for the benefit of a private company he controls is so blatantly corrupt and unconstitutional that it would have been hard to even fathom just a few years ago," said Seth Stern, chief of advocacy at Freedom of the Press Foundation, a plaintiff in the case along with news outlet The Intercept.

Trump Media said selling fast access to traders is common in its industry, and that the plaintiffs are just trying to silence the president ( AP Photo/John Minchillo )

Trump Media said selling fast access to traders is common in its industry, and that the plaintiffs are just trying to silence the president.

“Information from President Trump is disseminated by countless platforms and news outlets, many of which offer subscription APIs," it said in a statement, using the acronym for the fast access service. "Now, left wing activists are trying to wrongfully weaponize the courts to censor him again and harm our shareholders.”

The early access service comes as the publicly traded Trump Media loses hundreds of millions of dollars each quarter and its stock has dropped below $10 from $62 shortly after going public two years ago.

The plaintiffs argue that Trump's deal giving exclusive Truth Social access to his posts for six hours before being distributed elsewhere violates two parts of the Constitution — the First Amendment right to access a president's comments on equal terms with other members of the press and public and the Fifth Amendment prohibitions on charging unreasonable conditions for government benefits.

The suit asks that Trump Media be forced to end both the new paid service, called Truth API, and its exclusive access deal with his company in general.

Even before the new API service was started earlier this month, ethics watchdogs criticized Trump's posting on Truth Social as a brash attempt to profit off the presidency in keeping with other money making ventures tarnishing the office, especially ones related to cryptocurrencies. Earlier this year, the president filed a required annual financial disclosure report that showed he took in more than a $1 billion last year from new crypto businesses that his administration regulates.

Among other moves since he was reelected, Trump's digital finance company, World Liberty Financial, got a $500 million investment from a company tied to the government of the United Arab Emirates and sold hundreds of millions of dollars worth of special souvenir Trump meme coins to his fans and possible federal favor seekers, included a billionaire fighting a federal law suit that was later paused, then settled.

In addition to the president, the lawsuit filed in the Southern District of New York names his deputy chief of staff Daniel Scavino and his executive assistant Natalie J. Harp as defendants.

This article was originally published on August 18, 2025, and is being republished by The Independent as thousands of students receive their A-level results.

Mathematics at A-level is going from strength to strength. Maths is the most popular subject choice, and further maths, which is a separate A-level course, has seen the most growth in uptake. Despite this, concerns still remain about the mathematical skills of young people who do not choose to study maths after they are 16.

Students in England who have passed GCSE maths at grade four or above, but who are not taking A-level or AS-level maths, are eligible to take a core maths qualification.

Core maths was introduced in 2014-15 to attempt to remedy a lack in mathematics education after 16. But the number of entries remains well short of what they could be. Many students who would benefit from maths after 16 are not taking this subject.

A 2010 report from the Nuffield Foundation found that students in the UK lag behind their peers in other countries in participation in mathematics after the age of 16. Further research from the Royal Society and higher education charity AdvanceHE showed that, as a consequence, many were not well prepared for the demands of their university courses or careers.

Survey data has also found that over half of UK adults’ maths skills are low.

Many courses at university include mathematical or quantitative elements ( PA )

Many courses at university include mathematical or quantitative elements, but do not require AS or A-level maths for entry. These include psychology, geography, business and management, sociology, health sciences, biology, education and IT.

When many students have not studied mathematics since GCSE, this results in a lack of fluency and confidence in using and applying it.

Core maths consolidates and builds on students’ mathematical understanding. The focus is on using and applying mathematics to authentic problems drawn from study, work and life. This includes understanding and using graphs, statistics and tools such as spreadsheets, as well as understanding risk and probability.

Take-up remains low despite incentives – schools receive an additional £900 in funding for each student who studies core maths. In 2025, 15,327 students took core maths – a 20% increase on 12,810 entries in 2024, which is very encouraging. However, research from the Royal Society in 2022 found that fewer than 10% of the number of A-level students who were not taking A-level mathematics had taken core maths, which will not have changed significantly even with the current numbers.

Increasing enrolment

There remains a strong commitment from the government to increasing participation in mathematics after 16 in England through core maths. Many schools and colleges have embraced the subject, and universities have expressed support too.

However, a real incentive for teenagers to study this subject would be if it was rewarded in entry to university. Universities can allow students entry to a course with lower A-level grade profiles than normally required if they also passed core maths, for instance. But the number of universities making this kind of offer is low.

About the author Paul Glaister CBE is a Professor of Mathematics and Mathematics Education at the University of Reading. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license. Read the original article.

Schools and colleges need stronger signals from universities to induce them to offer students the opportunity to study for a core maths qualification, and to encourage their students to do so. Shifting today’s landscape to one where the vast majority of learners aged 16 to 19 in England are studying some form of mathematics which is relevant to their current and future interests and needs will require reform.

The Royal Society’s 2024 report on mathematical and data education sets out several reforms necessary to develop the mass mathematical, quantitative and data skills needed for the careers of the future. These include compulsory maths and data education in some form until 18. Extending the take-up of core maths would be an excellent way to begin achieving this.

Nurses are collapsing on shift while treating patients in conditions exceeding 30C, the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has warned.

With the UK on track for its warmest summer on record, nursing staff have suffered seizures and described "dripping with sweat from head to toe" while working.

Concerns have also been raised over patient welfare, with some hospitals described as "unbearably hot" and "not fit for humans".

RCN chief executive and general secretary Professor Nicola Ranger said: “When nursing staff are collapsing, feeling dizzy, sick or even being admitted to the very hospitals they work in because their workplaces cannot handle the heat, it shows just how badly they are being failed.”

The conditions nurses are facing during heatwaves

The RCN compiled a series of testimonies to its advice line, including:

– A nurse in England reported collapsing from dehydration after working a long shift on a ward with no ventilation. They were admitted to the same organisation where they worked.

– Pregnant nurses said the temperatures they were forced to work in impacted their health, while two nurses with pre-existing conditions reported seizures due to excessive heat.

– One nurse told the RCN their workplace was “not fit for humans” while another described their working environment as “unbearably hot”.

– Others reported broken air conditioning, fans or ventilation, with some reporting that they are unable to even open windows.

open image in gallery One nurse told the RCN their workplace was “not fit for humans” while another described their working environment as “unbearably hot” ( PA )

– Multiple nurses reported working in rooms where the temperature was in excess of 30C, with one saying they were forced to work in a place which was 36C.

– A nurse working in an NHS cancer service in England reported feeling “nauseous, dizzy and faint” after temperatures exceeded 33C.

– A nurse working in a community health centre in England said: “It gets to the point you dread going to work, especially when wearing PPE (personal protective equipment) and providing patient care. We drip with sweat from head to toe.”

– Others expressed concern for patients, with one saying the heat impacted surgical patients’ recovery while another said: “We have elderly patients in our clinic, who we are increasingly worried about. We have got to the end of our tether with no support from our immediate seniors.”

Prof Ranger said: “These testimonies should be a wake-up call.

“Swathes of the NHS and social care estate are in disrepair following decades of underinvestment and are utterly unprepared for extreme temperatures.

“It’s becoming an impossible and inhumane place to work or receive care, with vulnerable patients, including the elderly and those recovering from surgery, receiving care in temperatures that risk making them sicker. It’s unacceptable.

“Employers must also abide by their legal duties to make workplaces safe, by mitigating the risks to staff from the heat. This includes installing air conditioning, improving ventilation, ensuring water and heat-appropriate uniforms are available and guaranteeing risk assessments are a core part of business planning, especially for pregnant or vulnerable workers.

“We also need specific actions to protect those working in the community, who often are travelling in hot cars, with poor access to parking and left to walk long distances carrying heavy bags to meet patients.”

‘£100m to upgrade hospital buildings’

Meanwhile Matthew Hopkins, director of the NHS Alliance ambulance and acute network, said NHS organisations were pushing for increased capital money from the Government to deal with maintenance of hospital buildings.

Speaking on the NHS Alliance’s Health on the Line podcast, he said: “I think for a lot of our members that are running hospitals that are very old and where infrastructure’s really under pressure, many of those hospitals are carrying significant levels of backlog maintenance.

“Some of our members tell us that that totals, in some cases, more than £100 million worth of cost.

open image in gallery A nurse working in an NHS cancer service in England reported feeling “nauseous, dizzy and faint” after temperatures exceeded 33C ( PA )

“And inevitably, the boards of those organisations will be regularly discussing and focusing on the risk management associated with the trade-offs that they’re going to have to be dealing with, you know, fixing a roof of a building to make it safe and watertight for winter versus installing air conditioning and potentially the impact on the electrical infrastructure.”

It comes after the NHS has been ordered to prepare for the effects of heatwaves each year in the same way that it plans for winter by Health Secretary Yvette Cooper.

And earlier this year the Climate Change Committee of MPs said that the Government should ensure cooling measures are installed in hospitals and care homes by 2035, ranging from shading through to air conditioning.

Commenting, Ruth Wilkinson, head of policy at the Institution of Occupational Safety and Health, said: Indoor workers, like nurses, can find it just as challenging to work in extreme heat as outdoor workers.

“This can be due to poor ventilation, lack of cooling infrastructure, and outdated building designs that leave them to cope in stifling conditions.

“Heat stress can make it harder for people to work safely and effectively.

“When it’s too hot, the body has to work harder to stay cool, which can lead to health problems like dehydration, heat exhaustion, or even heat stroke.

“Employers can take proactive steps to manage these risks and support workers. These can include adjusting work hours, providing cooling stations, and encouraging hydration.”

The Department of Health and Social Care has been approached for comment.

Fly half Richie Mo’unga has been recalled to the New Zealand squad to leave head coach Dave Rennie with a major selection dilemma for the four-Test series against South Africa.

Mo’unga has not appeared for the All Blacks since starting the 2023 Rugby World Cup final defeat to the Springboks, with the playmaker subsequently moving to Japan and thus ineligible for international selection.

The 32-year-old has returned to New Zealand with Canterbury in recent weeks, though, and has now been summoned to the touring squad after centre Billy Proctor was ruled out with a shoulder injury.

Mo’unga will join up with Rennie’s group ahead of a meeting with the Bulls at Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria this weekend before the All Blacks take on the world champions in the first of four Tests in Johannesburg next Saturday.

“We really feel for Billy,” Rennie said. “He has had a great season so this is frustrating for him. It is the harsh reality of our game. We wish him all the best with his recovery and hope to see him fit and well in time for the end of year tour selection.

"Richie is the obvious choice as a replacement. His job now is to get in and learn our systems, get his head around the detail and earn the right to play."

Mo’unga’s return had been anticipated for the remainder of the Nations Championship in November, but comes ahead of schedule to bolster Rennie’s options.

open image in gallery Ruben Love has impressed for the All Blacks of late ( Getty )

Ruben Love has established himself as New Zealand’s first-choice fly half with three assured showings in the July Tests, and remains the favourite to wear the No 10 shirt at Ellis Park as the Springboks series begins.

Veteran Beauden Barrett and the versatile Damian McKenzie also provide alternative options, although Mo’unga had seized the shirt before his move to Japan and remains a high-class option.

McKenzie suffered an ankle injury in the midweek win over the Sharks in Durban, but it is hoped he will be fit to feature next weekend.

Britain’s economic growth slowed in the second quarter but a boost from record hot weather and the World Cup helped offset impacts from the Iran war in a better-than-expected performance in June, official figures have shown.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 0.4% between April and June, down from 0.6% growth in the first three months of the year.

Its data showed growth of 0.3% month-on-month in June, against expectations for a flat performance, as the ONS said firms across the services sector reported buoyant trade thanks to prolonged hot weather and the start of the World Cup football tournament.

The June rise in GDP followed flat growth in May, revised down from 0.1% growth previously estimated, and a 0.1% contraction in April.

Liz McKeown, ONS director of economic statistics, said: “Growth slowed in the second quarter of the year, following a strong start to 2026, but remained relatively robust.”

“Services also drove growth in June, with some businesses reporting that good weather and sporting events may have had a positive impact that month,” she added.

But the data comes amid worries over the impact of the Middle East conflict on the UK.

It emerged on Wednesday that Treasury experts have briefed the Prime Minister to expect the economy to barely grow next year if disruption to the Strait of Hormuz linked to the Iran war continues until the end of 2026.

Internal modelling from the Treasury suggests UK GDP could see growth as low as 0.3% in 2027, Government sources have said.

open image in gallery (PA Graphics) ( PA Graphics )

In response to the latest GDP data, Chancellor John Healey said: “I know people are worried about the impact of the conflict in the Middle East on their cost of living, which has been too high for too long and it has added pressure on British businesses.

“This is an active, hands-on Government, putting British interests first – giving breathing space to those feeling the strain, making our country more resilient and bringing hope back.”

The ONS said the services sector grew by 0.4% in June, though this was partly offset by falls of 0.2% in production and 0.1% in construction.

Food and drink firms were among those to benefit from the start of the World Cup on June 11, while television and advertising also benefited from the event, which saw the England team reach the semi-finals in July.

Hot weather also helped boots retailers, as well as some manufacturing firms, hotels and those in the amusement and recreation sector.

But the extreme heatwave, which saw three consecutive days of record-breaking June temperatures peaking above 37C, also knocked parts of the economy, with some construction firms reporting a hit, while in education, many schools were closed because of the heatwave.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle 1 Everton 3

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

Sports.title: Alisha Lehmann wears black bikini on beach trip with Love Island star fiance as he gets over non-league red card
Sports.content:
ALISHA LEHMANN has wowed in a black bikini during a beach trip with fiance Montel McKenzie.

The lovebirds took a trip down to sunny Brighton after McKenzie’s horror show for Whyteleafe against Burgess Hill.



McKenzie, 28, finished the 3-0 defeat early as he was sent off for arguing with the referee.

He was even mocked on social media by the Burgess Hill X account, who refereed to him as a “Love Island reject”.



The match had more bizarre goings-on as it had to be stopped after a GOOSE invaded the pitch.

A trip to the seaside proved to be a nice treat to get over the abysmal performance on the pitch.

He shared multiple pictures on his Instagram account of the relaxing break.

One picture showed himself and Lehmann, 27, posing for a selfie in an elevator.

The second snap showed the WSL star taking a dip in the sea off the pebbled beaches of Hove.

She could be seen wearing a black bikini while in the water, with the Rampion Offshore Wind Farm visible on the horizon.



Another picture uploaded by McKenzie showed the stunning open-well staircase of The Grand Hotel on Brighton seafront.



As well as being footballers, the couple also take part in the Baller League.

Lehmann is the manager of McKenzie’s six-a-side team, MVPs United.

The couple went public with their romance in January and things have moved quickly with an engagement.

They recently enjoyed a holiday in Lehmann’s homeland of Switzerland.

They took part in a traditional activity is known as “Aare Bootle” and floated down the Aare River together.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick gives strongest hint yet Marcus Rashford will stay at Man Utd after Leeds draw
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK has dropped a strong hint that Manchester United could keep hold of Marcus Rashford.

Rashford, 28, watched on from the sidelines as United battled Leeds in a pre-season friendly at Croke Park on Wednesday.



And he is expected to get a run-out against AC Milan this weekend.

There were points where it looked like there was no way back for Rashford at Old Trafford, having spent last season on loan at Barcelona and half of the campaign before that at Aston Villa.



But he has been welcomed back into the first-team fold by Carrick after Barca opted not to make his loan move permanent.

And after watching his side beat rivals Leeds on penalties after a 1-1 draw in Dublin, the United boss fed speculation that Rashford could stick around for the upcoming season.

He said: “He’s our player. He’s come back great. He’s just like any other player.

“I’ve known Marcus a long time and he gives us something a little bit different.

“He’s been in great spirits since he’s been back. He’s been back two or three days, trained, and it’s just pretty normal, to be honest.

“We’re looking forward to the start of the season.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Rashford boasts 138 goals in 426 United games but has not played a competitive match for the club since December 2024.

Whether he gets the chance to add to those tallies remains to be seen.

United star Noussair Mazraoui was also put on the spot about Rashford’s future.

He said: “He could be a big one [new signing] for us this season. That is, of course, if he doesn’t leave.”

Sports.title: Chelsea give Man City til 5pm Friday to complete £120m Enzo Fernandez transfer as Barcelona’s £55m Rodri bid rejected
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have told Manchester City they have until 5pm on Friday to seal a £120million deal for Enzo Fernandez.

The Blues vice-captain has been publicly pushing for a move away from the club since March, having flirted with Spanish giants Real Madrid.



Former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca, who has replaced Pep Guardiola at the Etihad, is keen on Fernandez.

Man City are keen to sign a replacement for Rodri, should the World Cup winner leave.



Rodri is desperate to move to Barcelona but City have rejected a bid of £55m from the Catalans.

City value him at £70m but there is a feeling in Spain they can be persuaded to do business if bidding goes over £60m as he has less than a year left on his contract.

And Chelsea’s deadline for Fernandez is likely to strengthen Barca’s hand in negotiations amid fears Maresca could be left without a star midfielder.

Enzo Fernandez criticised Chelsea for their decision to sack ex-boss Maresca in an interview conducted while on international duty in March.

However, the Blues will not budge on their £120m asking price and have informed City that if it is not met before 5pm on Friday, then he will be staying at Stamford Bridge.

Should the worst come to the worst, Elliot Anderson believes he has some of the same qualities as Rodri, so could help fill the gap in midfield.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

England star Anderson, 23, said: “Yeah, I can be quite similar. I can do various things within midfield.

“I’ll play anywhere — creating, driving forward or the other role.”

New Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has said he wants Fernandez to remain at the club.

However, deals for a replacement have been explored in case the 25-year-old were to leave.



Bournemouth rejected a £64million deal for Alex Scott earlier in the window and while the Blues have not returned with another offer, their interest in the England man remains.

City have also explored a move for French defender Malo Gusto.

Chelsea are open to selling the right-back following the arrival of Marco Palestra from Atalanta, however they have placed a £75m asking price on him.

Sports.title: ‘Diver’ Elliot Anderson reveals unique Haaland welcome to Man City after crushing team-mate’s World Cup dreams
Sports.content:
ELLIOT ANDERSON laughed off Erling Haaland calling him ‘The Diver’ as the club-record signing took the plunge at Manchester City.

The new team-mates clashed at the World Cup during England’s quarter-final showdown with Norway in Miami.



Haaland thought Norway had taken a second-half lead only for Torbjorn Heggem’s ‘goal’ to be ruled out by VAR after the striker’s push on City’s £116million signing Anderson in the build-up.

Nearly four weeks on, Haaland showed he had not forgotten the flashpoint, referring to Anderson as ‘The Diver’ on social media.



However, there was no ill feeling as both players reported for pre-season training yesterday.

Asked if he had seen his new team-mate’s post, Anderson, 23, said: “Yeah, it went viral. He’s been calling me a diver!

“It was funny. He has been really good today and has helped me settle in.

“He’s been spot on with me — a really good guy.”

The Three Lions went on to win the last-eight tie 2-1 – only to go out in the semis as Argentina staged a late comeback.

Ex-Nottingham Forest midfielder Anderson has had three weeks off but admits he is still not over the nature of that Atlanta exit.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

He added: “It’s really hard. I’m still sort of struggling with that.

“There are highs and lows in football. It’s about how you bounce back.

“I’ve had three weeks to reflect on it but now is a new season.

“But I take huge confidence knowing I can perform on a World Cup stage.”



Anderson briefly became the most expensive British player of all time this summer — only for England team-mate Morgan Rogers to take the record when he joined Chelsea a few days later.

The City new boy, 23, said: “The fee always will be mentioned. As long as I focus on myself and my performances, that’s all I can do.

“I’m sure I can show people what I can do. But I’m good friends with Morgan, I’m delighted he got the move he wanted.”

Anderson was also chased by Manchester United but never had any doubts he wanted City. And not even Pep Guardiola’s May departure could change his mind.

Anderson said: “I’ve been watching City for the past ten years or so.



“Pep leaving didn’t affect me at all. It’s such a huge club and the players they have are the best.

“I wanted to be surrounded by these sort of players, proving myself on a daily basis.

“I’ve done a bit of work with (City boss) Enzo Maresca on my first day and I’m really looking forward to more — you can see the details he goes into.”

As for United’s interest, he added: “I knew about it. You’ve got a big decision to make — and I’m confident I’ve made the right one.”

Before signing for City, he bumped into former United stars Ryan Giggs and Phil Bardsley while playing golf in Portugal.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

They tried to turn his head towards the red side of town but Anderson said: “We had a nice chat, I had a decision to make and I chose City.”

Asked if they had come close to changing his mind, the new Etihad star said firmly: “No”.

Sports.title: ‘Cannot be at our peak’ – Matthias Jaissle issues urgent transfer plea and reveals fears for Newcastle in Liverpool game
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE’S issued an urgent plea for new signings after Newcastle’s 3-1 thumping by Everton.

Harvey Barnes’ consolation failed to stop Thierno Barry, Iliman Ndiaye and Tyrique George condemning the German to a first defeat in the job.



Despite officially only being in charge a week, the 38-year-old admits his team will struggle to be ready to face Liverpool in the Prem opener unless he gets exactly what he needs.

Jaissle said: “For sure, we cannot be at our peak [against Liverpool], this is clear. We have just been working for a couple of days together, and Liverpool is already next week now.



“We use every day in the best possible way, that’s the only thing we can control to make progress.

“Then, it will be the same with the transfer market. Hopefully, there will be progress there too.

“We have already spoken about it in the press conference, and I think everybody has seen the matches and are smart enough to see the needs in the squad.

“I will always be consistent with my approach – we handle these things internally.

“We are aware of what we need, and as you know, there is still some time.

“It is not a case of just wishing for things to happen and then they happen – that is not the case in football or in life.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“But internally, we are really clear.”

Newcastle have just over ten days to go until they face Liverpool.

Jaissle acknowledged at his official unveiling on Tyneside he has inherited a “vacuum” of leadership in his squad.



But 24 hours later in Edinburgh, it was errors from two of the most experienced players left that sparked this bruising defeat to the Toffees – without new signing Brennan Johnson and Jarrad Branthwaite (hamstring rehab).

And as the skies eerily darkened over Murrayfield, so did the mood within the Toon Army.

Jaissle knows any hopes of eclipsing predecessor Eddie Howe’s success rest on what happens before the window closes in 19 days.

Barry pounced on a wild swing from Dutch defender Sven Botman, 26, to eventually break the deadlock, despite Manchester United target Lewis Hall’s best efforts, with his third of pre-season for Everton.



Then Brazilian midfielder Joelinton’s clumsy challenge on Kiernan Desbury-Hall allowed Ndiaye to double the lead from the spot before the break.

George brilliantly left midfielder Sean Steur, one of the three outfield signings this window aged under 20, for dead with a spin to rifle home a third.

Jacob Murphy teed-up Barnes, two of Howe’s trusted lieutenants, late on but it did little to lift the gloom.

Jiassle hopes to have Benfica full-back Amar Dedic, 23, on board before his St. James’ bow against Leverkusen on Saturday.



And asked if he was confident sporting director Ross Wilson would deliver what he wanted this month, he added: “It’s not a wish concert, not in football, not in life.

“But again, internally we’re really clear.

“There could be because there are still a couple of days to go, but it’s not in my hands.”

Sports.title: PSG 2 Aston Villa 1: Villans left to rue missed chances as Madjo, 17, nets in Uefa Super Cup but Doue has final word
Sports.content:
IN the heart of Red Bull country, Aston Villa did not get the lift-off they sought for their latest chapter.

They were not given the famous wings everyone talks about around here – but nor did they have theirs clipped.



And, even in defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, Unai Emery will be heartened by what the future may hold after speaking positively about a “new era”.

This was the fourth Super Cup defeat of the Spaniard’s managerial career and he will wonder quite how.



Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue struck either side of debutant Brian Madjo, 17, to secure the win for PSG.

But Villa, and especially Madjo, had plenty of chances to make this another European night to remember.



Madjo hit the post during a pulsating end to the first half and there were shades of the Villa from recent seasons – the one that loved to blood the noses of Europe’s elite.

That is promising given the team picked for this season-opener in Salzburg was very different to the side that booked a spot in it.

Just five of the players that started the Europa League final in Istanbul were in the XI for this game, and there was the added blow of new signing Alejandro Garnacho missing out due to concussion.

Emery had decided to leave World Cup stars Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins out of the squad, giving them an extra week’s rest.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And that made for a weakened side, especially after the summer departures of key trio Lucas Digne, Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans.

PSG, in contrast, went strong, with nine of the 11 that beat Arsenal in May’s Champions League final starting.

Fabian Ruiz and Ousmane Dembele were the two to miss out, with new signing Maghnes Akliouche and Warren Zaire-Emery replacing them.

With these two sides just coming to the end of their pre-seasons, there were plenty of loose touches and passes on show in the opening stages.



But the one man who did not look rusty was Kvaratskhelia.

After a summer off where he was watching the top stars shine at the World Cup, the Georgian looked in the mood.

And it was his goal after 20 minutes that broke the deadlock, with a stinging shot leaving Villa keeper Marco Bizot no chance.

It was made by a lovely shimmy from Kvaratskhelia – showcasing hip movement that Shakira would be proud of – and the Villa defenders were left for dead.

PSG tried to kick on from there and a stunning clipped-pass from their star winger set left-back Nuno Mendes away, but no one was there to turn home the cross.



The floodgates did not open for the French side and, instead, Villa roared back into the game.

Madjo was excellent up top, bullying defenders and demonstrating why he cost £10million from Metz in January.

Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors meant he was unable to play until now after a successful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport earlier this month.



And we will surely see plenty of him this season after his goal levelled the game on the stroke of half-time.

John McGinn’s excellent cross to the back post made it and you could not argue that it was more than Emery’s side deserved.

It was a goal that will be remembered for some time.

Firstly, because Madjo became the youngest player to score in the Super Cup, overtaking Patrick Kluivert who was 19 when he bagged in 1996.

And secondly, because a Villa fan went viral on social media for celebrating it with a moony.



Before that it was Madjo feeling red-faced after missing some great chances. He had gone close with a header from another wicked McGinn delivery and struck the post after a rampaging run that left PSG defenders on the floor.

On another day, he could have had a hat-trick and Villa would have been in dreamland.

PSG had the luxury of throwing on Dembele at the break as they tried to regain some control.

It was his France team-mate Doue, however, that put the Champions League holders back in front just after the hour mark.

The winger’s curling effort was originally ruled out for offside, but VAR intervened to reignite the pyro party behind the PSG goal.



Villa were not disheartened by that and debutant Joao Gomes came close to an equaliser with less than 20 minutes to go.

The bench brought energy, too, with Alysson’s cross somehow not turned home by Tammy Abraham when the goal was gaping.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And even right at the death there was one more chance. This time it was Emi Buendia heading wide.

But Luis Enrique’s side held on to become only the second team in history to retain the Super Cup.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Myles Lewis-Skelly shows why Gunners MUST keep him but Gabriel Jesus should be first out of door
Sports.content:
MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY scored a crucial goal to see Arsenal’s pre-season end in victory over Como, with a 1-1 draw being decided by penalties after Alvaro Morata missed from the spot in the shootout.

He opened the scoring by capitalising on a horrific piece of goalkeeping by Jean Butez in the Como goal, cushioning the ball with his head before planting it in the bottom left corner.



Perhaps the most pleasing part of the goal for Arsenal fans will be that he celebrated by forming a heart with his hands to the Gunners in the stands amid rumours that he could be leaving.

Martin Baturina levelled things before half-time, with a wonderful cut onto his right foot before finding the roof of the net – something he seems to like doing to English fans after scoring against the Three Lions at the World Cup.



Bruno Guimaraes impressed on his Arsenal debut in the second half, in which Kai Havertz thought he had found a late winner, only for it to be offside.

With the score level at 1-1, a penalty shootout decided things

This is how SunSport reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 6

Made one save in the first half before being replaced by David Raya.

Wasn’t massively tested and couldn’t do an awful lot to stop Martin Baturina’s fine leveller.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

THEO JULIENNE – 6

The youngster was really impressive at right-back, offering composure on the ball and solidity in his tackling against a really exciting young winger in Assane Diao.



Found it more tricky against Martin Baturina when he moved to the left and some will blame him for the goal, but he was still impressive.

MARLI SALMON – 8

Really solid at the back for such a young defender, he didn’t look any worse than Gabriel next to him, which is perhaps the biggest compliment you could pay him.

Good on the ball, won more duels than any other Arsenal player, and always on hand to sweep up when his side needed him – plays like a defender twice his age.

GABRIEL – 6

Really good on the ball when playing out from the back, he was physically dominant and solid in defence as ever.



PIERO HINCAPIE – 6

Impressive on the ball at left back, but could have done more in terms of supporting Martinelli going forwards.

Solid though at left back with a number of good tackles, interceptions and recoveries.

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 8

After a week full of rumours linking him with a move away from the Emirates, he formed a heart with his hands when he was gifted a goal by Como keeper Jean Butez.

If Manchester United or Chelsea were watching this one, they might be a little more interested now after a good all-round midfield showing.



EBERECHI EZE – 7

Played a slightly deeper midfield role than usual, but was still very involved going forwards, coming close with a free-kick early on and being at the heart of most good things from Arteta’s side.

That was until he was hooked early on by Arteta and replaced by Fabio Vieira.

MAX DOWMAN – 6

Really exciting to watch on the right side and you could see flashes of his quality and quick feet.

He was well marshalled most of the time by two or three Como defenders, but still managed to impress in glimpses – it’s easy to forget he is so young.

ETHAN NWANERI – 6

Looked really engaged early on with some great tackles and some really tidy footwork, but more often than not that final bit of end product evaded him.



GABRIEL MARTINELLI – 7

Claimed the assist for Myles Lewis-Skelly‘s opening goal, but was good all round in his play today, with some silky dribbles and bursts of pace down the left side.

GABRIEL JESUS – 4

Seemed to have missed a sitter early on, only to have his blushes spared by the offside flag anyway – that was until he too was hooked early on for Viktor Gyokeres.

That was his only real chance, with limited involvement in the game, but he wasn’t overly impressive by any means.

SUBS:

VIKTOR GYOKERES (GABRIEL JESUS, 32) – 5

Didn’t do an awful lot while he was on the pitch, but he wasn’t on it for a very long time.



A few decent bits of hold up play, but not much else to talk about without much support around him.

FABIO VIEIRA (EBERECHI EZE, 32) – 5

Similarly to Gyokeres, he didn’t have an awful lot of time on the pitch to impress.

A few decent passes and glimpses of his dribbling ability on the half turn, but nothing to write home about.

BRUNO GUIMARAES (MAX DOWMAN, HT) – 7

Already a fan favourite at the Emirates after making a few tackles and some nice passes on his debut.

Chants of “Bruno, Bruno, Bruno” could be heard loud and clear for their new dynamic midfield man, who anchored the Gunners midfield nicely with some great defensive play.



Scored his penalty in the shootout too.

DAVID RAYA (KEPA ARRIZABALAGA, HT) – 6

Did exactly what was expected of him, making a simple save in the second half and being good with his feet.

CRISTHIAN MOSQUERA (GABRIEL, HT) – 6

Almost gave Arsenal the lead with an early second half header that was saved by Butez in the Como goal.

Looked quick and sharp at the back, ready to step up in William Saliba‘s absence if called upon.



MARTIN ODEGAARD (ETHAN NWANERI, HT) – 6

Kept things ticking for Arsenal but struggled a little in terms of creating chances for those around him.

Plenty of good passing and a few nice dribbles but nothing in terms of the end product required to win his side the game.

RICCIARDO CALAFIORI (MARLI SALMON, 60) – 6

Not really caused any problems at the back, but dealt with any Como threat nicely, perhaps should have been more involved going forward when his side needed a goal.

KAI HAVERTZ (VIKTOR GYOKERES, 60) – 7

Came close to giving his side the lead in the second half, but no cigar with a left footed shot that fell wide of the post.

Then thought he’d scored a last-gasp winner with a fine finish, only for the linesman to raise his flag and curtail the celebrations.



Still, he was creative and caused more problems for Como than Gyokeres or Jesus.

MIKEL MERINO (PIERO HINCAPIE, 60) – 6

Plenty of touches, with some good passing and defensive contributions, but is another player who has match-winning moments in him who couldn’t find one today.

NONI MADUEKE (FABIO VIEIRA, 60) – 6

Another who came close to finding a winner for Arsenal, but was just missing that end product required of him.

He was more creative than most in this game with the ball at his feet, but played it safe a little too often.



It felt like everyone in the stadium knew he was going to miss in the shootout.

CHRISTOS TZOLIS (GABRIEL MARTINELLI, 60) – 6

Not overly impactful from the left, particularly when Martinelli had been quite exciting to watch in spells – didn’t see an awful lot of the ball.

Gets a bonus point for his emphatic winning penalty.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

BEN WHITE (THEO JULIENNE, 60) – 6

Pretty much identical to Calafiori on the other side, solid defensively, but not showing enough going forward with the scores level.

JOSH OGUNNAIKE (MARLI SALMON, 88) – N/A

Not enough time to make an impact.

Sports.title: Gold medallist Thomas chases 'own legacy' after AJ comparisons
Sports.content:
Commonwealth Games gold medallist Damar Thomas wants to create his "own legacy" after being compared to former Team GB super-heavyweight stars following his triumph in Glasgow.

The boxer followed in the footsteps of Joe Joyce, Frazer Clarke and Delicious Orie when he beat India's Narender Berwal via unanimous decision to win gold in the super-heavyweight category.

Standing at 6ft 6in, Thomas has earned inevitable comparisons with Anthony Joshua and represents one of the great hopes for the future of British heavyweight boxing.

The 21-year-old, who is targeting success at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, is unfazed by such comparisons and insists he is focused on his own development.

"Yeah, it's a great feeling [to win gold]. I managed to add my name to the British heavyweights that won the Commonwealth [gold]," he said.

Image: Thomas is aiming for gold at the LA Olympics in 2028

"Hopefully in LA I'll be able to add my name to those great heavyweights that managed to get Olympic gold.

Image: Thomas brushed off comparisons with Anthony Joshua

"I'm just in my own race at the minute and taking it in my own strides. I'm not comparing myself to anyone. I'm doing everything at my own pace, which is great. What I want to do is create my own legacy, which is a good feeling."

Thomas demonstrated significant boxing IQ in his 5-0 victory over Berwal, marking his 11th consecutive win in a run that extends back to November.

"My main asset is my feet and my speed," Thomas said.

"That's what works for me with these heavyweights, because a lot of these heavyweights rely on one shot. I don't rely on that, so it's great."

Image: Thomas has not lost a fight since November 2025

While Thomas' main ambition for now is to remain amateur and win gold in LA, he has his sights set on becoming a professional after the games in 2028.

"First, I want to tick off that box with LA. I'm taking one tournament at a time," he added.

"It's a marathon, not a sprint. And I'm just taking everything at my own pace.

"The main goal is the Olympics. Until then, I'm thinking about Olympics and nothing else. But after the Olympics, I'll definitely turn professional."

Sports.title: Jodar's bid for history halted in Nakashima defeat as Rybakina beats Gauff
Sports.content:
Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar's bid for ATP Tour rankings history was put on hold after he was beaten by Brandon Nakashima in the semi-finals of the Canadian Open.

Jodar, 19, had been hoping to make history in the Montreal for the fastest rise into the top 10 of men's tennis but his attempt to make a first Masters 1000 final was ended in straight sets by American Nakashima.

Nakashima, the 28th seed, had never previously made it past the third round at the tournament but was too strong for Jodar in a 7-6 (7-3), 6-4 triumph.

Jodar saved four match points before Nakashima finally converted his fifth to overcome the world No 15 in two hours and two minutes of play on IGA Stadium.

"Going into the tournament, I knew I was playing at a really high level, so I knew that I could get a go on a deep run here," said Nakashima.

"Obviously, wasn't thinking about the final or anything."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Ben Shelton against Learner Tien from the Canadian Open.

Nakashima will face defending champion Ben Shelton in an all-American final on Friday, live on Sky Sports Tennis.

Shelton beat compatriot Learner Tien in the night's second semi-final and said afterwards: "Super happy with the performance.

"Learner is a guy who presents me with a lot of problems in my game. A tough challenge to overcome.

"To get a win over him in the fashion that I did, I'm super pleased with that."

Rybakina fights back to beat Gauff to set up Swiatek final

At the women's semi-finals in Toronto, second-seeded Elena Rybakina beat fourth-seeded Coco Gauff 5-7, 6-2, 6-2 to book her place in the final.

Rybakina will play seventh-seeded Iga Swiatek on Thursday night after the Pole saw off ninth-seeded Elina Svitolina 6-3, 1-6, 6-3.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Windsor and Lingfield feature on Thursday
Sports.content:
Windsor and Lingfield play host to Thursday evening's action - live on Sky Sports Racing.

7.41 Windsor - Law Court and City Of Poets head the field

Law Court and City Of Poets clash with an in-form trio in the RIP Susan Procter Memorial Handicap.

City Of Poets was building a progressive profile before slightly disappointing in the Coral Challenge on Eclipse day last month. He was partially hampered that day and the form of that race is very strong, so the drop back in class and step up in trip may see James Tate's representative bounce back to form.

A similar angle applies to Law Court, who ran on in a slowly-run competitive mile handicap at Glorious Goodwood and will certainly hold strong claims up in trip. His previous two showings at Sandown, which included a victory on Brigadier Gerard night, would give backers confidence going into this assignment.

In-form trio A Major Payne, Bold Impact and Parlando all won nicely last time out and remain on potentially handy marks, with the first runner winning in particularly taking fashion over the course and distance. That performance suggests the rise in class should not prevent him from staking a bold claim under Billy Loughnane, who is chasing his maiden jockeys' championship crown.

King's Code cannot be ruled out back down in class considering his Chester success last month, as Auld Toon Loon returns to his last winning mark over course and distance last August after finishing a creditable eighth in the John Smith's Cup.

Box To Box may find it tough on firmer ground after 11 months off the track, although he does remain on a competitive mark.

7.11 Windsor - Waterford Castle opposes Amo's expensive recruit

The highly-tried Waterford Castle pitches himself in calmer waters, facing Amo Racing's Partying - who was bought for 4.4m guineas - in the Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting UK Racing Maiden Stakes.

The George Boughey-trained Waterford Castle is the only horse in here with a rating and comes to Windsor a 10-race maiden. The base form would suggest he is not very good but he has arguably just bumped into quite a few nice types in ultra-competitive races thus far.

His first two starts this year resulted in being turned over at odds-on, but the winner of the second contest won a valuable race at Sandown subsequently. This gelding finished second behind future Shergar Cup winner Archers Bay and managed to finish in mid-division in Royal Ascot's King George V Stakes - which reads very well given the winner Enceladus has since won a Group Three and the second Al Azd bolted up at Ascot next time out (earning a rating of 109).

The fly in the ointment could be Partying. This Frankel filly out of Aljazzi is an unknown quantity and should be watched in the market on debut. Of the others, Thatcham could be of interest returning from a break. Richard Hannon's charge was never in the race at Southwell the last day but could fare better on turf with Pat Dobbs booked.

7.28 Lingfield - Shangri La opposes Neswick

Shangri La opposes the eye-catching Neswick in Lingfield's Become a Friend of Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes.

The Kirsten Rausing-owned three-year-old bids to break her maiden tag following a creditable reappearance at Wolverhampton, where she placed fifth on handicap debut. This daughter of St Mark's Basilica could benefit from the step down in trip with Callum Shepherd in the plate. Her breeding suggests she will both do better at middle distances and develop with age and she sets the standard, dropping back into a novice.

The John and Thady Gosden-trained Dove Tale improved on her first start at three just a week ago, managing to place under Rab Havlin at Kempton. A half-sister to German Derby runner-up Diamond Dove, this filly could have more to offer.

Despite Neswick's modest pedigree, she shaped extremely well over course and distance on debut and can provide stiff opposition, especially if coming on for the run.

Best of the rest

Remaining at Lingfield, Kaaranah seeks a hat-trick in the opening Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap (5.23pm). John Butler's charge has been nudged up 4lb to a mark of 74 but could go in again up against the likes of Alice De Clare and Barbury Boy.

At Windsor, the well-handicapped Great Chieftain aims to get back on track up against Colourband in the Matchbook Loves Racing Handicap (6.41pm) before Mythological Star looks to record a third consecutive win in the Classic Golden Music Group 10th Anniversary Handicap following a success at the track on Monday.

Sports.title: Where would Antonelli rank among surprise F1 title winners?
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli is on course to become Formula 1’s youngest-ever world champion, but where would the Mercedes driver’s triumph rank among the sport’s biggest surprise title wins in recent history?

With the 2026 season having reached its summer break, Antonelli has defied expectations to build a 50-point advantage over Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in second, ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix from August 21-23.

The 19-year-old Italian has won six of this season's first 11 grands prix, and his advantage makes him the clear favourite to remain at the top of the standings when the 12 remaining scheduled rounds are complete.

Antonelli's lead would have been even greater had it not been for an engine blowout in Barcelona and wheel-guard failure at Silverstone costing him a major haul of points.

However, there's still a huge amount of work to do for Antonelli to claim the title, with Mercedes' early-season dominance having faded as Ferrari and McLaren combined to win three of the last five races before the break.

Antonelli will not only have to contend with potentially not having the fastest car on the grid during the second half of season, but also the pressure of attempting to close out the capture of a maiden title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli claims his debut win for Mercedes at the Chinese GP

Why would Antonelli winning be a surprise?

At the start of this season, Antonelli had never won an F1 race. The highlights of the 19-year-old's rookie campaign had been a Sprint pole in Miami and grand prix podium finishes in Canada, Brazil and Las Vegas.

Having been fast-tracked into one of F1's most desirable seats to replace the Ferrari-bound Hamilton at the start of 2025, Antonelli endured a rookie campaign that left many questioning whether he was the generational talent Mercedes insisted they had unearthed.

Even if, as it appears to have been the case, some of Antonelli's struggles last year were down to inexperience and the all-round challenge of being an F1 driver rather than any lack of talent, few envisioned him as the 2026 world champion.

The main reason for that was the perceived strength of his team-mate George Russell, who had more than held his own alongside seven-time world champion Hamilton during their three years as team-mates, before outscoring Antonelli by 319-150 points in 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli jumps in Monaco harbour, celebrating his fifth consecutive win of the 2026 Formula 1 season

Therefore, even if Mercedes met expectations by delivering the strongest car following F1's rules reset for 2026. It seemed highly unlikely that Antonelli could make a big enough leap over the winter to be able to get the better of Russell over the course a full season.

There was also the fact that even if Antonelli could find a way to beat Russell, the likes of Hamilton, four-time world champion Max Verstappen and reigning world champion Lando Norris were - and are - all waiting to pounce on an opportunity.

Add into the mix that the youngest world champion in F1 history is currently Sebastian Vettel, who won his first title when he was 23 years and four months old, and it just seemed like a far-fetched idea that Antonelli, who turns 20 later his month, could be ready.

As Antonelli continues his quest for glory, here are some of the drivers who have previously upset the odds to become a world champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli wins the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix

Fernando Alonso, Renault - 2005

Similarly to Antonelli, Fernando Alonso was regarded as a star of the future going into 2005 but nobody expected him to dominate in the fashion he did, wrapping up the first of two titles with two races to spare.

Alonso had won just one race prior to 2005 but Renault became serious front-runners thanks to a key regulation change which outlawed tyre changes at pit stops.

The Spaniard built an early season lead as Renault won the opening four races and capitalised on his main championship rival, McLaren's Kimi Raikkonen, suffering reliability issues.

Image: Fernando Alonso won both of his world titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006 (Associated Press)

Alonso's team-mate Giancarlo Fisichella could not cope with the sheer speed of the then 24-year-old, who became the youngest world champion in F1 history at the time.

Michael Schumacher had won the previous five drivers' titles but 2005 felt like a passing of the baton and Alonso confirmed that by also winning the 2006 championship.

Image: Michael Schumacher had won his seventh world title the year before Fernando Alonso became world champion in 2005 (Associated Press)

Jenson Button, Brawn - 2009

Perhaps the biggest surprise in F1 history is the memorable 2009 season where Jenson Button and Brawn became world champions.

Partly due to the 2008 financial crisis, Honda surprisingly left F1 so Button, team-mate Rubens Barichello, team principal Ross Brawn and chief executive Nick Fry were left without jobs.

Brawn and Fry bought the team for £1 to create Brawn GP before doing the unthinkable - designing and creating a car which started the season as the benchmark.

Image: Jenson Button led a one-two from Brawn GP team-mate Rubens Barichello at the first race of 2009 in Australia (Associated Press)

Button, who had only won one race at the 2006 Hungarian Grand Prix, and Barichello claimed a remarkable one-two at the season-opening.

The British driver triumphed at six of the opening seven races before budget limitations saw Brawn's rivals reel them in as the season progressed.

Nevertheless, Button held on to win the title ahead of Red Bull's Sebastian Vettel, before Brawn GP was bought by Mercedes over the following winter.

Image: Jenson Button secured the 2009 world title at the penultimate race in Brazil (AP Photo/Silvia Izquierdo)

Nico Rosberg, Mercedes - 2016

Having beaten Mercedes team-mate Nico Rosberg to the title in 2014 and 2015, Lewis Hamilton was the clear favourite to become a four-time world champion in 2016. However, Rosberg had other ideas.

Although Hamilton only won the 2014 title at the last race, things were significantly more comfortable in 2015 as he wrapped up the championship with three races to spare.

Very few believed Rosberg could beat Hamilton over the course of a season but everything came together in 2016 for the German to come out on top.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton backed up Nico Rosberg at the 2016 Abu Dhabi decider

He won the opening four races, while Hamilton struggled to get on top of his car. Rosberg also capitalised on his team-mate's reliability issues to build a 23-point lead with five rounds remaining.

By winning the Japanese Grand Prix, it meant Rosberg could finish second at the last four rounds and still be world champion. By then, he started to think about retiring if he achieved his dream so the pressure was sky-high.

Hamilton won the final four races and attempted to back up his team-mate at the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, but Rosberg held on to finish second, which was enough to secure the title.

Sports.title: MI London's Hundred title defence over despite narrow win over Phoenix
Sports.content:
MI London had the lights turned out on their hopes of claiming a fourth straight Hundred title despite beating bottom-placed Birmingham Phoenix in a nip-and-tuck final men's group match.

As the Edgbaston crowd were treated to a solar eclipse, the visitors knew they needed to win by at least 59 runs to take third position from SunRisers Leeds and qualify for the play-off on their home patch after Phoenix won a crucial toss and elected to field.

A total of 157-6 meant they would progress if they could restrict Phoenix to 98, and three wickets in the powerplay put a spring in their step, Sikandar Raza clean bowling Joe Clarke and Richard Gleeson dismissing Mitchell Owen and Laurie Evans with consecutive deliveries to pull clear as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 14 victims.

However, a solid partnership between Jake Weatherley and Sean Dickson steadied the ship and a Tom Curran wide took Phoenix to 99 and ended MI London's slim hopes.
