Clearly, FSSAI has bowed to food industryâs interests,â said Dr Arun Gupta of Nutrition Advocacy in Public Interest (NAPi).

FSSAI stated in the affidavit that it had held a stakeholder consultation on March 19, 2026 involving consumer groups, food industry representatives and farmer organisations. It stated that industry bodies argued that âconsumers should be able to make an informed decision without creating fear amongst the consumersâ. The affidavit was silent on the input given by consumer organisations, which had sought warning labels that have been shown to be the most effective in reducing consumption of junk food high in salt, sugar and saturated fats in several countries.

NAPi had also given FSSAI evidence generated from studies conducted in India and other countries showing how effective warning labels are.

World.title: Govt notifies Rs 3,030-crore scheme for three mega chemical parks
World.content:
The Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan) scheme, announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27, was cleared by the Cabinet chaired by PM Modi.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has formally notified the BHAVYA Rasayan scheme to establish three greenfield chemical parks across the country, paving the way for states to compete for projects aimed at boosting domestic chemical manufacturing, reducing import dependence and attracting investment.The Gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers operationalises the scheme approved by the Union Cabinet last month. With a total outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, the scheme will run from 2026-27 to 2030-31 and support the creation of shared industrial infrastructure for the chemical sector.Under the scheme, the Centre will provide up to Rs 1,000 crore for each chemical park, subject to the concerned state contributing at least Rs 500 crore. Any expenditure beyond this will have to be borne by the state government. Each park must have a minimum 8 sq km (2,000 acres) of contiguous, encumbrance-free land.The parks will be selected through a challenge-based competitive process, with proposals evaluated on predefined quantitative and qualitative parameters, including strategic relevance, financial viability, implementation plans and long-term sustainability.According to the notification, the parks will provide common facilities such as central effluent treatment plants, hazardous waste management systems, water supply, solvent recovery and distillation units, steam generation and distribution networks, interconnected pipelines, logistics infrastructure, laboratory testing centres and emergency response facilities, enabling industries to reduce costs and improve environmental compliance.The government said the scheme is aimed at strengthening the entire chemical value chain, enhancing domestic production capacity, improving cost competitiveness, promoting exports and import substitution, attracting domestic and foreign investment, and generating employment, while contributing to the goal of Viksit Bharat 2047.

World.title: From New York to Delaware: US states to commemorate 'India Day' on August 15
World.content:
Delaware has proclaimed August 15, 2026, as âIndia Dayâ, joining New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day and the contributions of the Indian-American community ahead of the country's 80th Independence Day.

The proclamation was issued by Delaware Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community and its contributions to the state's social and economic life.

The development was shared by the Consulate General of India in New York on August 13.

According to the proclamation, Delaware is strengthened by the many cultures and traditions represented across its communities, including its Indian-American population.

Delaware honours Indian-American community

The proclamation said Delawareans of Indian heritage have enriched the state through their work, leadership and service, contributing to shared prosperity and creating opportunities for future generations.

It also highlighted India's diversity of languages, traditions, faiths and customs, noting that generations of Indian Americans have carried these traditions forward while building communities in the US.





The proclamation said India Day would provide an opportunity to honour India's independence, celebrate the heritage and achievements of Delaware's Indian-American community and recognise the enduring connections between Delaware and the people of India.

Governor Meyer encouraged residents to participate in the observance and recognise the contributions of the state's Indian-American community.

New York, New Jersey also recognise August 15

Delaware's proclamation follows similar declarations by New York and New Jersey, which recognised August 15, as India's Independence Day.

New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill issued a proclamation recognising Indian Independence Day across the state. According to the Consulate General of India in New York, the proclamation highlighted the Indian-American community's contributions to New Jersey in areas including education, healthcare, research, technology, business, public service and community leadership.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state.

The Consulate said New York's proclamation recognised the Indian-American community's contribution to the state's cultural, economic and civic life, while also highlighting the enduring ties between India and the US.

The Consulate thanked Hochul for the recognition, saying the proclamation celebrated India's journey of independence and the democratic values shared by the two countries.

How US communities celebrate India's Independence Day

India's Independence Day is marked across the US each year through flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural programmes and community events.

Indian diplomatic missions, including the Embassy of India in Washington and Indian consulates, hold special programmes on August 15. The Indian mission to the United Nations also participates in commemorative events.

Indian-American communities across states organise cultural performances and public celebrations, with local political leaders often participating and highlighting the community's contributions to American society.

Prominent landmarks have also joined the celebrations in previous years, including the Empire State Building in New York and the Space Needle in Seattle, which have been illuminated in the colours of the Indian tricolour for Independence Day events.

India marks 80th Independence Day with focus on youth

The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.

This year's celebrations will also focus on the commemoration of 150 years of âVande Mataramâ, while placing particular emphasis on âYuva Shaktiâ or youth power.

The celebrations are expected to combine the historical significance of India's freedom movement with recognition of the achievements and contributions of its younger generation.

The growing number of US states formally recognising India's Independence Day also underlines the visibility of the Indian-American community and the broader social, economic and cultural ties between India and the United States.

World.title: Al-Qaida offshoot AQIS behind Red Fort blast in 2025: UNSC report confirms
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has officially attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhiâs iconic Red Fort to Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), according to the 38th report of its Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team.

The attack on November 10 last year claimed 11 lives.

"Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS, not listed) continued to evolve from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist entity; it established logistics and financial networks, working in decentralised, small, scattered cells instead of large units. The attack in November 2025 on the Red Fort in Delhi was officially attributed to AQIS," the report, published on August 10, stated.

The assessment marks a significant shift in the attribution of the Red Fort attack, which had earlier been linked to the Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM).

The report noted that one member state had attributed a series of attacks to JeM and also linked the group to the Red Fort blast.

The explosion occurred around 7 pm when a moving Hyundai i20 erupted in flames near the iconic monument.

Investigators identified Umar-e-Nabi as the driver of the car and suspect him of carrying out the attack as a suicide bomber.





Read also:

Launched in 2014, AQIS is a regional affiliate of Al-Qaida.

The group was formed to expand the organisationâs activities across South Asia, including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and parts of Afghanistan.

Meanwhile, the latest UNSC assessment also flagged broader concerns over the activities and capabilities of Al-Qaida and Islamic State (ISIL/Daâesh) affiliates.

It also highlighted the widespread circulation of instructions on producing such agents in online terrorist communities.

World.title: Supreme Court pushes 19 states, union territories to notify cancer
World.content:
Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With the National Cancer Registry Programme covering only a fraction of Indiaâs population and rural cancer surveillance remaining particularly limited, the Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so, a move that could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.Such notification could help plug gaps in cancer surveillance by giving health authorities a more complete picture of the countryâs cancer burden, including where cases are rising and which populations are most affected. The data could in turn help shape policies on prevention, early detection, treatment capacity and allocation of healthcare resources.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant passed the order on a plea filed by a retired AIIMS doctor after his lawyer Gaurav Bansal told the court that NCRP covers only 10% of population and rural coverage is less than 1%.The push assumes greater significance against the backdrop of the WHOâs latest Global Status Report on Cancer, which estimates that 92% of people globally will be affected by cancer either directly or through a close family member.The report also projects annual cancer cases to rise to nearly 35 million by 2050.The Supreme Court was informed that 17 of Indiaâs 36 States and UTs have already notified cancer, following recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The remaining 19 have now been asked to consider similar action.Dr Pragya Shukla, Head of Clinical Oncology at Delhi State Cancer Institute, said standardised, disease-specific and timely data was essential to track India's changing cancer burden, identify regional and demographic trends, and assess the impact of prevention and treatment programmes. Such a system, she said, would complement existing cancer registries, help identify high-burden areas, improve planning for treatment infrastructure and medicines, and strengthen evidence-based cancer control. Govil added that reliable data would be critical for planning prevention, early detection and resource allocation.The Indian Cancer Society welcomed the intervention, saying national notification could help build a comprehensive cancer surveillance system. âThe Supreme Courtâs intervention is a significant development, and we welcome its direction to the remaining States and Union Territories to move towards cancer notification,â said Jyotsna Govil, Chairperson, Indian Cancer Society, Delhi. However, she stressed that notification alone would not suffice and called for a uniform national framework with common definitions, reporting standards and data protocols to ensure comparable and interoperable data across states.

World.title: FSSAI puts influencers, celebrities on notice over food promotions
World.content:
FSSAI warns influencers of legal action over unverified food claims

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From "boosts immunity" to "rich in nutrients", food claims endorsed by celebrities and social media influencers are now under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) scanner. In a significant move aimed at curbing misleading promotions, the regulator has warned influencers and celebrities that endorsing unverified food claims could invite legal action, even as it cracked down on manufacturers selling unsafe food products.The advisory comes at a time when food brands are increasingly relying on digital creators and celebrities to market health drinks, protein supplements, snacks and packaged foods to millions of consumers online. FSSAI has asked influencers to verify that every claim made by a brand is truthful, scientifically substantiated and compliant with food safety regulations before lending their name or credibility.The regulator said endorsements are more than s because consumers often trust the people promoting them. It cautioned influencers against amplifying claims such as "boosts immunity" or "rich in nutrients" unless they are backed by evidence and permitted under food laws.Misleading food s and endorsements, it said, can attract action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.Alongside the advisory, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, sale and distribution of food products made by M/s Shree Shyam Foods, M/s Bharat Food Products and M/s KDP Food Industry after government laboratories found their ghee and mustard oil products unsafe for consumption.The regulator also penalised Dharwad Mishra Pedha and Food Processing Industry in Karnataka after its Motichoor laddoos were found to contain Tartrazine at 2,670.5 mg/kg, more than 26 times the permissible limit of 100 mg/kg. Shree Chemfood Pvt Ltd of Gujarat was similarly penalised after samples of iodised salt were found to be substandard and misbranded.FSSAI has also urged consumers to report misleading food s and celebrity endorsements through its Food Safety Connect platform.

World.title: Actor Vikram case: Farm owner in Erode asked to produce documents on Lar Gibbons
World.content:
The Erode Forest Division has asked the owner of an animal breeding farm in Perundurai to produce the registration certificate and other documents relating to two Lar Gibbons (Hylobates lar) found at his facility during an inspection by officials of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), Chennai, and the Forest Department.

K.V. Appala Naidu, District Forest Officer, Erode, told The Hindu the registration process for the animals was incomplete and the owner had been asked to produce the required documents on August 14. Though he had produced certain documents, there were some shortcomings. The documents sought included the registration certificate obtained by the Manipur-based owner from whom the animals were purchased, Mr. Naidu said. Details had also been sought regarding the death of a female Lar Gibbon that had not been reported to the authorities, as reporting such an incident is mandatory under the Living Animal Species (Reporting and Registration) Rules, 2024, he said.

The inspection of the farm owned by K. Keshavanathan followed a video posted on social media by Tamil film actor Vikram in which he was seen petting and hugging a Lar Gibbon. The video went viral and drew criticism from wildlife activists over the possession of an endangered species without the requisite documents. The actor later removed the video. The Lar Gibbon is listed in Appendix I of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

What the probe found

The inquiry revealed industrialist C.K. Ranganathan of Erode had purchased two Lar Gibbons from the farm owner and moved them to Chennai. Mr. Ranganathan is the father-in-law of Mr. Vikram’s daughter. Further inquiry revealed that the farm owner had purchased the animals from Manipur and brought them to Perundurai.

Under the regulations governing exotic live species, an owner is required to register with the Forest Department, declare the stock in his possession, and report the acquisition of any new animal within 30 days. Only after the declaration is made will the facility be inspected by the Forest Department to verify compliance, following which a Form 3 Registration Certificate will be issued.

The animals arrived at Perundurai on June 5, 2025. However, the owner applied for registration only on August 9, 2025, and transferred the animals to Chennai on the same day. “There was a delay of more than two months,” Mr. Naidu said.

The DFO said the registration process remained incomplete and the Forest Department was examining the documents produced by the farm owner.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Trump 'low-key' bets on economic pressure against Iran
World.content:
Keeping a low profile doesn’t come naturally to Donald Trump.

Yet that is the strategy the American President says he now favors in the war against Iran, and he is betting on economic pressure over diplomacy or new strikes.

Also read | Do not write the obituary of international law yet

“We are low-keying it,” Mr. Trump told news site Axios by phone Sunday (August 9, 2026).

“We’re only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money.”

World.title: Withdraw circulars restricting workers from speaking to media, CITU tells Vizag Steel Plant
World.content:
Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) Andhra Pradesh State president Ch. Narasinga Rao on Thursday (August 13, 2026) condemned the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant management’s circulars of August 10, which restrict workers from sharing or forwarding plant-related information with the media.

Addressing a press conference in Visakhapatnam, Mr. Narasinga Rao and CITU State secretary R.K.S.V. Kumar alleged that the restrictions were aimed at suppressing workers’ voices, and sought the withdrawal of the circulars.

The union alleged that steel plant workers were owed ₹900 crore in salaries, and that the management held reserves of the same amount. It also alleged that skilled workers had been removed, that workloads had increased as a result, and that workplace accidents were continuing.

CITU sought the reinstatement of the contract workers who had been removed, and compensation of ₹1 crore for the family of each worker killed in the June 8 accident at the steel melting shop.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 19 LIVE: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die
World.content:
Both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha were adjourned sine die on Thursday (August 13, 2026), wrapping up a Monsoon Session that witnessed little transaction of business (with no Question Hour and several Bills being passed amid without debate) amid repeated disruption over Opposition’s protests on NEET paper ‘leak’, Ram Temple donations ‘theft’, Home Minister Amit Shah’s statement on police action on students’ protests, among others.

Also read: Kharge condemns ‘shuddhikaran’ after his Uttarakhand visit; J.P. Nadda expresses regret

The Lok Sabha was adjourned sine die shortly after the national song ‘Vande Mataram’ was played at the beginning of the last day. Both Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah were present. Meanwhile, the Rajya Sabha passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, following a discussion. The Upper House functioned for a total of 37 hours and 49 minutes, and 12 Bill were considered for passing or returning, Chair C.P. Radhakrishnan said in his closing remarks, expressing regret over the “persistent disorder” this session

Also read | 31-member parliamentary panel to review FCRA Bill

On Wednesday (August 12, 2026), Amit Shah said he was willing to have a full debate on the students’ protests against the NEET paper ‘leak’, while Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju stated that the government was ready to “increase the time” allotted for a debate on the issue. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, however, rejected the offer of a discussion, stating that the youth wanted answers on who ordered the firing on and police assault of protesters and “not a lecture” from Mr. Shah.

World.title: Recital of full version of Vande Mataram at UDF govt. swearing-in in Kerala kicks up a row
World.content:
The recital of the full version of Vande Mataram at the swearing-in ceremony of the United Democratic Front (UDF) in Kerala on Monday (May 18, 2026) has kicked up a row with the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] calling it a move that undermines secularism and pluralism and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)’s mouthpiece Organiser hailing it.

In a statement issued in Thiruvananthapuram on Tuesday (May 19, 2026), the CPI(M) State secretariat said that the Congress Working Committee itself had taken the stand that performing Vande Mataram in its entirety of six stanzas was unsuitable for a pluralistic society. Parts of the song were trimmed as part of the official resolution of the Working Committee held on October 30, 1937. On January 24, 1950, the Constituent Assembly had clarified that only the first eight lines of Vande Mataram should be performed as the national song.

World.title: Fresh clash erupts along Assam-Arunachal border, police fires in air to disperse mob
World.content:
A fresh clash erupted between protesters from Assam and Arunachal Pradesh in Dhemaji district on Thursday (August 13, 2026), forcing the police from the neighbouring State to fire in the air to control the mob even as the indefinite economic blockade against the Himalayan state entered its second day.

The Takam Mising Porin Kebang (TMPK), the apex student organisation of Assam's Mising community, and other local groups on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) launched an indefinite economic blockade against Arunachal Pradesh in protest against the alleged firing in which 12 indigenous people from Assam were injured.

"When the blockade was going on, some people from Arunachal Pradesh indulged in stone pelting on protesters from Assam and some persons sustained minor injuries. This led to a scuffle between the two sides," an official said.

The incident took place at Likabali entry point in Silapathar in Dhemaji district of Assam, he added.

"Then we saw that police from Arunachal fired three rounds in the air to control the mob on their side," the Assam government official said.

At least 12 people from Assam were injured on Monday (August 10, 2026) after alleged firing by miscreants from Arunachal Pradesh along the inter-state border in Dhemaji district over land encroachment issues.

Along with TMPK, other local social groups like Mising Mimag Kebang (MMK) and Takam Mising Mahila Kebang (TMMK) are supporting the blockade and stopped all vehicles, barring emergency and school transportation, from coming or going to Arunachal Pradesh at the entry points.

The organisations are demanding an early resolution of the Assam-Arunachal Pradesh border dispute, action against the "miscreants" who had fired two days ago and an end to alleged encroachment on Assam land.

As part of the agitation, protesters blocked key entry points along the inter-State border, including roads at Dwarmukh-Banderdewa, Ruksin and Silapathar in Dhemaji, Banderdewa in Lakhimpur, Solengi in Gohpur and Pabhoi in Biswanath.

TMPK secretary Saan Panging said, "Such incidents along the inter-state border are not new, but our government has not taken it seriously. This time, our agitation will continue till all the culprits are arrested and handed over to Assam Police." To hammer out a solution in respect to withdrawing of the economic blockade, Assam Border Protection and Development Minister Atul Bora and Education Minister Ranoj Pegu will hold a meeting with TMPK leadership at the Circuit House of Dhemaji.

Himanta appeals for peace along Assam-Arunachal border, says boundaries can never divide hearts

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Thursday appealed to both sides to maintain peace and said no boundary can divide the hearts of the people who have been living like brothers and sisters for generations.

“I appeal to the people of Assam and Arunachal to maintain peace and harmony. Boundaries may define our States, but they can never divide our hearts,” Mr. Sarma said in a post on X.

Tagging his Arunachal Pradesh counterpart Pema Khandu and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, the Assam CM said that the two Northeastern States share a bond that goes far beyond boundaries.

“For generations, our people have lived as brothers and sisters, bound by love, affection and mutual respect,” he added.

Mr. Sarma stressed that the two States in recent years have resolved most of their border differences through dialogue and friendship.

“Only 52 villages remain, and both Governments will continue discussions in the same spirit to resolve the dispute completely,” he added.

On Wednesday, Mr. Sarma said Mr. Khandu "must" order an inquiry into the incident and ensure that those responsible are punished.

Mr. Pegu, who was deputed by Mr. Sarma to monitor the situation along border, said Mr. Khandu has promised to ensure strict action against those responsible for firing along the inter-state border.

On August 10, the firing incident took place at Mingmang Basti along the Assam-Arunachal Pradesh border in Gogamukh revenue circle of Gerukamukh Police Station.

Police said the clash erupted following a dispute over alleged encroachment by people from Arunachal Pradesh on land in Assam.

Assam and Arunachal Pradesh share an 804.1-km border in Udalguri, Sonitpur, Biswanath, Lakhimpur, Dhemaji, Tinsukia, Dibrugarh and Charaideo districts, and 12 of the adjoining State.

There are 1,200 points of dispute along the inter-state border between the two States.

The Assam government on July 29 told the State Assembly that Arunachal Pradesh has encroached upon 16,144.01 hectares of land. Out of this encroached land, Arunachal Pradesh is claiming 858.91 sq km.

Both the States have constituted 12 regional committees for resolving the border disputes, and are taking steps to resolve these issues based on recommendations of these committees, which have jointly toured the areas and held consultations with stakeholders.

A Namsai Declaration was signed by the Chief Ministers of the two States on July 15, 2022, setting in motion measures to resolve differences in 123 villages of Assam claimed by Arunachal Pradesh.

An MoU in this regard was later signed by the two CMs in the presence of the Union Home minister in the national capital on April 20, 2023.

Out of the 123 villages claimed by Arunachal Pradesh, the differences in 71 villages have been resolved and the process is on to address the issues in the remaining 52 villages.

Arunachal Pradesh was a centrally administered region initially after Independence and became a Union Territory later, before attaining full statehood in 1987.

After Arunachal Pradesh achieved Statehood, a tripartite committee was appointed, which recommended that certain territories be transferred from Assam to Arunachal Pradesh. Assam contested this, and the matter is in the Supreme Court.

World.title: Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury asks Telangana govt. to oppose trans law amendments in Supreme Court
World.content:
Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury has written to Chief Minister Revanth Reddy of the Congress-led government in Telangana, asking that the State government take a position in the Supreme Court to support the Constitutional challenges to the recently passed amendments to the Transgender Rights law that removed the right to self-identification of gender identity.

The law, passed in Parliament this March, ran into widespread protests from the transgender community across the country and had also led to resignations from members appointed to the Government’s National Council for Transgender Persons over provisions that mandate medical certification of gender identity instead of relying on self-identification.

Ms. Chowdhury, whose opposition to the amendments has been vocal, inside and outside Parliament, has now asked the Congress government in Telangana to support the challenges to the amendment that are currently being heard in the Supreme Court of India. In a letter to Mr. Reddy, the Congress’ Rajya Sabha MP from Telangana said, “I would earnestly request the Government of Telangana to extend its support to these proceedings through the office of the Learned Additional Advocate General, Shri Rajnikanth Reddy, by assisting the court in defence of the constitutional rights and dignity of transgender persons.”

In addition to this, Ms. Chowdhury has also requested the Telangana government to “carefully examine the administrative, financial and implementation implications of the new Act” for the State. She noted that this was needed to look at where the amended Act “may conflict with the State’s existing welfare architecture and its commitment to protecting the rights of transgender persons”.

Ms. Chowdhury noted in her letter to the Telangana CM that the State has “consistently stood for inclusion, social justice, and constitutional morality, and its intervention at this stage would carry both legal and moral significance.”

She also noted that during the debate on the amendments in Rajya Sabha, the Congress party had strongly opposed the legislation on the grounds that it undermined the principles of dignity, equality, and self-identification recognised by the Supreme Court, and “strikes at the heart of the guarantees under Articles 14, 15, 19, and 21 of our Constitution”.

At the time the Bill was being introduced and discussed, a delegation of trans activists from across the country had also met with the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi and Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in New Delhi, following which the official account of the Indian National Congress had posted a statement saying that Mr. Gandhi reiterated that the “Congress party stands firmly with the rights and dignity of transgender persons and will oppose the Bill in Parliament”.

Soon after the amendments to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act were passed, several challenges to it were filed before the Supreme Court of India, which has issued notice in these matters to the Union government. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for August 17.

World.title: Predawn burglary at retired engineer’s house in Madanapalle; 670 grams of gold stolen
World.content:
Burglars struck the house of a retired Rural Water Supply (RWS) Department divisional engineer at the Postal and Telecom Colony on the outskirts of Madanapalle in Annamayya district in the early hours of Thursday (August 13, 2026), and took away gold, silver and cash.

The Madanapalle police said the burglars cut the window grilles and entered the house while the occupants were asleep. They reportedly broke open an almirah and stole around 670 grams of gold jewellery, two kg of silver articles and ₹25,000 in cash. The theft came to light when the family woke in the morning.

The police from Madanapalle I Town and the crime station reached the spot and began an investigation, besides deploying a clues team and a sniffer dog. CCTV footage from the neighbourhood is being checked. A case has been registered on a complaint by the house owner, Ravindra.

World.title: Norway commends Pakistan's 'constructive role' in US-Iran conflict
World.content:
Norway on Thursday commended Pakistan’s “important and constructive role” to mediate between the United States and Iran amid the Middle East conflict.

The development came as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held delegation-level talks with Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide, who arrived in Islamabad earlier in the day, the first such visit in a decade.

“Both sides reviewed the whole gamut of bilateral cooperation in various fields, including trade, investment, climate change, maritime affairs and education. They recognised the important role of the Pakistani diaspora in Norway and agreed to strengthen people-to-people ties between the two countries,” the Foreign Office (FO) said.

The two sides expressed satisfaction at the warm and cordial state of Pakistan-Norway relations and agreed to further deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” it said.

The FO said the two sides also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments of mutual interest.

“The Norwegian foreign minister commended Pakistan’s important and constructive role during the recent Iran-US conflict, including the leadership and contributions of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, DPM Dar and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir,” it said.

In televised remarks, Eide appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote peace and expressed Norway’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties.

He said Norway and Pakistan had a “very strong bilateral partnership”, adding that the presence of a large Pakistani community in Norway, which was “well integrated into Norwegian society”, had helped strengthen ties between the two countries.

“There are many leading politicians in Norway and many close colleagues who are actually of Pakistani-Norwegian descent, so it has really made a mark,” he said.

Eide said business ties between the two countries were also growing, particularly in the energy and fertiliser sectors, with Norwegian companies increasingly looking at opportunities in Pakistan.

He said Norway also saw opportunities for Pakistan to strengthen economic relations through its cooperation with Switzerland and Iceland, noting that the three countries could provide further avenues for expanding business relations.

Turning to the regional situation, Eide strongly commended the actions taken by Pakistan’s leadership, including the prime minister and foreign minister, in efforts to promote peace in the Middle East.

Eide described the ongoing war as “incredibly dangerous” for global peace as well as the world economy, and praised Pakistan for stepping forward. He also appreciated Pakistan’s role in facilitating the Islamabad talks and maintaining engagement with the parties involved.

“I think it is fair to say that the position of Pakistan on the world stage, also in peacemaking, has really been strengthened by this commitment,” he said.

Eide said Norway was ready to assist Pakistan’s peace efforts, noting that Oslo had experience in peace negotiations and maintained open dialogue with both Tehran and Washington.

“Wherever we can be useful, we will,” he said.

He also highlighted Norway’s experience in international maritime affairs, saying the country was among the world’s major seafaring nations despite its relatively small population.

He said Norway could therefore play a constructive role in discussions concerning international maritime law and developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Dar, Eide discuss bilateral ties

Earlier, the two ministers held a “restricted-format meeting”.

“DPM Dar warmly welcomed Eide to Pakistan. The two ministers discussed the full range of bilateral relations, as well as regional and international developments, and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation in all areas of mutual interest,” it said.

Upon his arrival in Islamabad, Eide was received at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary (Europe) Ambassador Ayesha Ali.

In a statement on Wednesday, the FO said the minister is undertaking the visit from Aug 13-14 at Dar’s invitation. During the visit, the two will hold delegation-level talks covering the full spectrum of Pakistan-Norway relations, it said.

“The two sides will discuss avenues for further expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, climate change, renewable energy, education and people-to-people contacts.

“They will also exchange views on important regional and international developments,” it added.

It said that the visit would build on high-level engagement between the two countries, including phone conversation between Dar and Eide in March and April, and the visit of Norway’s State Secretary Andreas Motzfeldt Kravik to Islamabad in May.

The FO stated that the visit would provide an opportunity to “further strengthen the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and Norway and to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation”.

World.title: SHC orders formation of committee to probe HIV outbreak among children at Karachi hospital
World.content:
KARACHI: The Sindh High Court (SHC) directed the provincial government on Thursday to constitute a committee for an “independent, impartial and comprehensive” inquiry into the HIV outbreak among children at Karachi’s Kulsum Bai Valika Hospital.

A two-member SHC bench, headed by Justice Adnanul Karim Memon and comprising Justice Muhammad Jaffer Raza, issued the directive as it announced its reserved judgement on a plea seeking an independent inquiry, registration of a case and lifelong medical treatment as well as appropriate compensation for the affected children.

The outbreak was initially reported late last year, following which the Sindh government carried out screening at the Sindh Employees Social Security Institution (SESSI)-run hospital located in Karachi’s SITE area. According to data shared by the Sindh government, at least 78 children have been found infected with HIV at the hospital while a screening in the nearby area also confirmed 120 additional cases.

But Advocate Tariq Mansoor, the lawyer who moved the SHC on the matter, claimed in his petition filed in May that the total number of infected children is around 200.

The court observed in its order on the plea that the departmental proceedings and reports submitted so far had been “insufficient to determine the number of affected persons, the source and circumstances of transmission, compliance with infection-control protocols and the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, as well as the supervisory and individual responsibility of the officials concerned”.

Keeping this in view, the court deemed it necessary “in the interest of justice, transparency and public confidence that an independent fact-finding mechanism be constituted by the competent authority, without expressing any final opinion regarding the guilt or innocence of any individual”.

It directed that a committee, headed by the Sindh chief secretary, be constituted. The chief secretary should co-opt two senior officers not below the rank of BS-20 and “preferably having no direct administrative involvement in the affairs of the hospital or the proceedings under inquiry” to join the committee, the court order stated.

The court directed that the committee should determine:

The actual number and particulars of children and other patients who were found HIV-positive and who received treatment at the hospital during the relevant period

The source, circumstances and possible mode of transmission of HIV, based on available medical and scientific evidence

Whether any disposable syringe or other medical equipment was reused, improperly disposed of, inadequately sterilised or otherwise used in violation of the applicable law, rules, protocols or standard medical practice

The existence and implementation of infection-prevention and control protocols at the hospital

The procurement, supply, storage, distribution and use of auto-lock, auto-destruct or auto-break syringes and the relevant record

The role and responsibility of medical, nursing, technical, administrative and supervisory officials concerned

Whether any officer or official, by act or omission, failed to discharge a statutory, administrative or supervisory duty

The status and legality of the departmental proceedings already initiated against the 37 officials and whether such proceedings adequately address the actual responsibility of the persons concerned

Whether any provision of the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, or any other applicable law has been violated and, if so, the persons responsible

The measures required for preventing recurrence of any such incident in the future

The court order further stated that the committee should be empowered to examine all relevant records, including medical and laboratory reports, screening data, procurement and stock registers, syringe records, duty rosters, infection-control and inspection reports, inquiry proceedings, CCTV footage where such incidents occurred in Sindh and other material necessary for an “objective determination, while affording a fair opportunity of hearing to any person against whom an adverse finding is proposed”.

The committee should submit its comprehensive report to the competent authority, as well as the SHC, within two months of its constitution, the order read. It elaborated that the report should identify “the factual position and, where supported by evidence, fixing responsibility and recommending appropriate departmental, statutory or criminal action pursuant to Section 7 of the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010”.

Pending the inquiry, the Sindh chief secretary should ensure through the relevant departments and SESSI that all affected HIV-positive children and other identified patients receive “comprehensive, uninterrupted and appropriate medical treatment”, including medicines, investigations, counselling and follow-up care, entirely free of cost, at any institution of higher standard as medically appropriate, the court ruled.

“All such expenses shall be borne by the government/SESSI and shall not be recovered from the affected patients or their families, and the arrangement shall continue for as long as medically required,” the court directed.

Noting the “extraordinary circumstances of the case and the vulnerability of the affected children”, the court further directed the provincial chief secretary to determine and process the “entitlement of each affected child/ family to compensation, financial assistance or other lawful relief, strictly in accordance with the applicable statutory framework and government policy”.

The chief secretary should ensure that the process is completed expeditiously and without unnecessary hardship to the affected families, the order said.

Moreover, the relevant authorities should ensure that no affected child or family is discriminated against, stigmatised or denied medical, social or other lawful assistance on account of HIV status, the court ruled, adding that the identity and medical information of affected children should be dealt with strictly in accordance with applicable law and accepted medical standards relating to confidentiality.

The court further directed the chief secretary and the health department secretary to ensure immediate preventive and corrective measures at Kulsum Bai Valika Hospital to eliminate any further avoidable risk to patients and strict compliance with the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, infection-prevention protocols and other applicable health regulations.

Where necessary, they should also ensure the framing of requisite rules in accordance with law, the court order added.

The court also observed that the matter concerned the protection of the rights to life, health, dignity and fair treatment and warranted an independent, transparent and evidence-based inquiry.

“The matter cannot be treated merely as an administrative issue, as the constitutional obligation to protect life under Article 9 [of the Constitution] extends to ensuring effective discharge of public-health and medical-safety responsibilities, particularly towards vulnerable patients,” the court order read.

However, it added, “allegations or departmental proceedings cannot by themselves establish individual culpability, which must be determined based on evidence and after due opportunity of hearing”.

Show-cause issued to petitioner

The court order also stated that during a hearing, the petitioner, Advocate Mansoor, “raised his voice and instigated the private persons accompanying him, prima facie to attract the media and allowed the private persons to record videos in court, which is a contemptuous act on their part”.

The act, the court observed, disrupted proceedings and “seriously disturbed the decorum and dignity of the court”.

“The unruly conduct of the petitioner and the persons in the shape of a mob present in court compelled this court to retire to chambers to complete the order, although almost the entire order had already been dictated in open court.

“Prima facie, the petitioner, being dissatisfied with the conclusion of the matter, attempted to obstruct the court from proceeding further in accordance with law,” the order read.

It added that the incident also exposed a “serious security lapse” on the part of the in-charge of court security, including the relevant deputy superintendent of police and senior superintendent of police.

They were also called upon to explain their position, and they sought time to hold an inquiry.

“Prima facie, they are directly responsible for maintaining order and security within the court premises. Their apparent negligence and failure to discharge their duties enabled a mob brought by the petitioner for his convenience to enter the courtroom, indulge in hooliganism and flagrantly disregard the authority and decorum of this court. Such conduct amounts to an unacceptable interference with the administration of justice, for which the petitioner and the persons acting with him must be held responsible in accordance with law,” the order read.

Therefore, the court directed that Mansoor be issued a show-cause notice, seeking an explanation as to why criminal and contempt of court proceedings may not be initiated against him.

The order stated that the petitioner should submit his written reply before the next date of hearing in separate contempt proceedings, either personally or through counsel, and to continue appearing in person on each date unless such appearance is dispensed with by this court.

“The representatives of the Sindh High Court Bar Association (SHCBA) and the Sindh Bar Council (SBC) were also called upon to intervene in the matter, who also sought time to call upon the petitioner for such misconduct and are also directed to be in attendance in the proceedings,” the order said, adding that the court office should place this matter before the SHC chief justice.

The bench also directed the SHCBA and SBC to take immediate and appropriate remedial measures in accordance with law, including coercive measures against the apparent misconduct of the petitioner.

Meanwhile, court security officials should identify the private persons involved in the incident and initiate appropriate proceedings against all those responsible, the bench directed.

It further instructed the court registrar to preserve and secure the CCTV/ video recordings of the areas inside and outside the courtroom so that the persons involved may be identified and appropriate action may be taken strictly in accordance with law to “secure and preserve the dignity of the court”.

World.title: Taliban support fuels deadlier TTP attacks in Pakistan: UN
World.content:
• Taliban chief reportedly warned outfit to halt attacks or risk losing support

• UN report points to training links involving TTP, BLA, Al Qaeda

• ISIL-K attacks decline in Afghanistan, but increase in Pakistan

ISLAMABAD: The Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group, according to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report.

The report also points to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

The 38th report of the UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team, covering the period from Dec 16, 2025, to June 9, 2026, said that “cross-border attacks between Pakistan and Afghanistan escalated, provoked by a high number of attacks by Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakis­tan against Pakistan”.

Like previous editions, the report was unequivocal in its assessment of Kabul’s role, saying that “the de facto authorities (Taliban) continued their support to the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which escalated attacks against Pakistan, provoking military exchanges”.

It noted concern among member states that the continuing conflict could create opportunities for terrorist groups and generate additional security challenges for the region.

Taliban’s dual-track approach

The assessment nevertheless recorded some initial steps by the Taliban authorities to contain the TTP, although these appeared aimed more at managing the group than dismantling its infrastructure.

The report said Afghan authorities had relocated around 2,000 TTP fighters and their families from areas along the Pakistani border to deeper inside Afghanistan in an effort to rein in the group.

It also said Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada had warned the TTP leadership through backchannel communications to halt attacks against Pakistan or risk losing Taliban support.

The developments point to what appears to be a dual-track Taliban approach, continuing to provide the TTP space and support because of shared ideological ties while moving some fighters away from the border to reduce attacks on Pakistan, avoid a major escalation with Islamabad and address growing international concerns.

For Pakistan, however, relocating fighters deeper inside Afghanistan would do little to address the underlying problem as long as the TTP’s command, training and logistical networks remain intact.

Meanwhile, the TTP has continued to expand its organisational structure and operational reach.

The report said that following its annual rahbari shura in December, the group announced a revised structure with two new divisions covering Balochistan and the central region, and Kashmir and Gilgit.

The restructuring also included a new division described by the group as the “TTP Air Force”, suggesting an effort to broaden its operational capabilities.

In March, the group announced in several languages its spring campaign, “Operation Khyber”, calling for increased attacks against Pakistani security forces and civilians.

One of its deadliest attacks during the reporting period came on Feb 16 in Bajaur, where a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device martyred 11 security personnel and a child and wounded others. The TTP claimed responsibility and was reportedly operating from Afghan­istan, the report said.

Blurred lines

The UN assessment also points to increasingly blurred lines between terrorist groups operating in and from Afghanistan.

Al Qaeda’s official media outlet, As-Sahab Media Foundation, issued a statement on April 28 supporting the Taliban and, for the first time, backing the TTP in its operations against Pakistan.

The report said that while Al Qaeda had previously provided ideological guidance, training and support to the TTP, the latest statement represented more direct backing.

“One member state reported that BLA terrorists were trained along with TTP by Al Qaeda trainers in Afghanistan,” it said.

The report also noted that Al Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) formed the backbone of Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan, which was reportedly involved in several attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

AQIS leadership was reported to remain in Kabul after being issued tazkiras, suggesting “close cooperation between the Taliban and AQIS”, according to the report.

The assessment thus points towards a wider militant ecosystem rather than an isolated TTP problem, with training, facilitation and logistical networks increasingly cutting across organisational boundaries.

ISIL-K remains another major component of the threat. The report described it as the greatest threat to the Taliban authorities and the region, despite serious setbacks suffered as a result of counterterrorism operations by Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban.

ISIL-K was reported to have moved its operational infrastructure towards northern Afghanistan while dispersing training networks across the Pakistan-Afghanistan border region, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and retaining a presence in the suburbs of Kabul.

The UN report said ISIL-K was in a rebuilding phase, having shifted from attempts to hold territory to conducting fewer but high-profile, mass-casualty attacks, demonstrating resilience and adaptability.

Member states reported that the group possessed modern tactical equipment, including drones, night-vision devices and thermal imagers, and had received training in urban combat and the use of drones.

One member state also reported that ISIL-K and the BLA shared facilitation networks for logistics.

The report said ISIL-K attacks had declined in Afghanistan but increased in Pakistan.

On Feb 6, a suicide bomber detonated explosives during Friday prayers at the Khadija Tul Kubra Mosque of the Shia community in Islamabad, killing 32 people and injuring more than 150. The attack was claimed by a group calling itself ISIL in Pakistan but was likely conducted by ISIL-K, the report said.

The group also claimed responsibility for the May 5 assassination of Pakistani cleric Sheikh Muhammad Idrees in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The findings suggest that the threat facing Pakistan from Afghanistan is becoming more complex, with the TTP retaining Taliban ideological and logistical support, Al Qaeda providing training and ideological backing and ISIL-K and the BLA benefiting from overlapping facilitation networks.

The Taliban’s reported relocation of TTP fighters and warning to its leadership may reduce immediate pressure along the border, but the UN assessment does not suggest that Kabul has taken the more consequential step of severing its relationship with the group.

Published in Dawn, August 13th, 2026

World.title: Gas supply to parts of Balochistan suspended after main pipeline blown up in Bolan
World.content:
QUETTA: The gas supply to several towns and cities of Balochistan, including parts of the provincial capital, was suspended late on Wednesday after a main gas pipeline in Bolan area of Kachhi district was blown up by unidentified miscreants.

The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) confirmed the incident and said that the 18-inch wide gas pipeline was badly damaged, disrupting the supply.

A statement by its spokesperson said that the explosion occurred at the KMP-246 Valve Assembly in the Bolan riverbed area near Gorkat, around 700 to 800 metres from the main Quetta-Sibi Road.

It said that unknown people planted explosives under the pipeline in the riverbed and detonated it with a remote control.

The company said the gas supply was suspended to Kolpur, Mach, Mastung, Kalat, Pishin, Ziarat and many parts of Quetta and added that consumers may face reduced gas pressure or supply.

Local sources said unidentified individuals allegedly targeted the main valve of the gas pipeline with explosives in the Daraz Bent area of Bolan. Following the explosion, flames and smoke were seen rising from the damaged pipeline.

SSGC said that teams were ready to initiate repair work, but they were waiting for security clearance before going to the affected area. The gas utility said its management was closely monitoring the situation and working to restore supplies as soon as possible.

In May, the gas supply to a vast area of the province was suspended after unknown armed men blew up a gas pipeline in the Dera Bugti area. The same month, the supply to Sohbatpur district in the Nasirabad division was also suspended after unidentified miscreants blew up a gas pipeline.

A similar incident also occurred in March as unidentified armed men blew up the main gas pipeline at Western Bypass area.

World.title: US senators demand inquiry into conditions aboard aircraft carrier deployed in Middle East
World.content:
Congressional Democrats demanded answers on Wednesday about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, following reports of food shortages, broken plumbing and mental health crises during the aircraft carrier’s record-setting deployment.

In a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Wednesday, Senator Richard Blumenthal called for the Navy to account for conditions aboard the aircraft carrier, which “has been deployed more than 250 days” without coming ashore “in over 200 days, setting a record for consecutive days at sea.”

Blumenthal voiced concern for such extended deployments, noting “widespread reports of shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns” and other problems aboard the Lincoln.

Senator Ruben Gallego called for “an official oversight visit with the bipartisan Senate Delegation to the USS Lincoln to investigate the reported alarming conditions,” in a post on X.

The USS Abraham Lincoln departed San Diego, California on November 21, 2025 for duty in the South China Sea and was rerouted to the Middle East before US-Israeli attacks on Iran that began February 28.

In two recent meetings, family members clashed with Navy leadership over the difficult conditions — including food shortages — faced by the 5,000 sailors and Marines aboard the Lincoln and demanded to know when loved ones would return home, MSNOW reported.

Some reported severe mental health issues and attempted suicides on board.

“The stories of crew members threatening to jump off the ship are a frightening alarm bell as to how bad the situation has become: moldy showers, sporadic hot water, rationed meals and soap, broken toilets, and grueling 12- to 16-hour shifts with no days off,” Gallego wrote in his post on Wednesday, adding that he has served in active duty himself.

“The way (US President Donald Trump) is treating our service members as he carries out this illegal war is not just disgusting, it’s dangerous.”

The US Navy did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

World.title: Emails reveal Indian carmakers' fuel contamination worries before public retreat
World.content:
Hours after India made public assurances last week that its ethanol-blended petrol was safe, the country’s main auto lobby withdrew a complaint about fuel contamination it had sent to the government a week earlier. The group said some figures needed more checks.

But separate communications between industry executives, reviewed by Reuters, showed that in the preceding days, top automakers Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors and Mahindra discussed their concerns about contamination of petrol blended with 20 per cent ethanol, called E20.

Their data compiled the most comprehensive fuel testing done by the industry since Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government started rolling out E20 nationwide from last year to help curb pollution and cut oil imports.

With no other petrol available since April 1, consumer concerns have grown about the impact on vehicle performance.

The carmakers’ emails show for the first time how they are privately worried about contaminants in E20, like chloride and moisture, which they say are hurting vehicles, even as they publicly back the government’s rollout of the fuel.

The Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) withdrew its July 28 letter on fuel contamination after a government and public uproar over the warning, saying “some numbers” need “authentication”.

The previously unreported industry data and emails reviewed by Reuters show “multiple” automakers had already conducted extensive tests by collecting over 250 fuel samples from pumps over a year from as many as 21 of India’s 36 states and territories. They found high chloride contamination in many of the samples in 18 states, as well as high moisture content.

The executives’ emails raised no concern about data authentication.

Asked for comment on the private emails, SIAM told Reuters the data was intended only for internal circulation, discussion and validation, and collected by “very few” automakers.

Maruti, Tata and Mahindra, who were part of the SIAM internal emails seen by Reuters, account for 67pc of India’s car market.

As “the testing basis and sample size were insufficient to support definitive conclusions, the communication was withdrawn” as it was sent inadvertently, SIAM said, adding it intends to undertake a proper scientific study.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas did not respond to requests for comment. Its minister, Hardeep Singh Puri, said on Friday that two weeks prior to receiving the letter from SIAM, India’s oil marketing companies had begun “rigorous testing” of fuel at retail outlets to check for contamination.

Only four cases of contamination were found, he said. State-run fuel retailers also said last week that extensive random and scientific tests showed “no cause for any alarm on account of fuel contamination”.

Mahindra said conclusions drawn from its executive’s emails “are completely baseless and incorrect”, industry data is limited and preliminary, and it does not see issues with E20. Maruti and Tata did not respond to requests for comment.

Auto industry met government to flag Chloride concerns

E20 has angered motorists, with hundreds alleging it has reduced mileage and increased wear and tear on their cars, and triggered at least one court challenge.

SIAM had earlier said high levels of chloride are corrosive for auto parts, while high moisture levels in fuel can immobilise a vehicle immediately after fuelling.

In the group emails exchanged among Maruti, Tata, Mahindra and SIAM, Maruti’s senior executive Anoop Bhat raised concerns on the high chloride findings, saying this had been privately discussed with the petroleum ministry on July 26.

The tabulated state-wide findings shared by the industry on group emails showed they recorded chloride levels of 6 to 570 parts per million (ppm) in Rajasthan state, 1.4 to 420 ppm in the capital New Delhi and 10 to 357 ppm in Maharashtra.

The Indian government says the permissible limit is 3 ppm.

The data tables also showed moisture levels reaching 13,000 ppm in Andhra Pradesh and 12,500 ppm in Uttar Pradesh, versus a permissible government benchmark of 3,000 ppm.

While the reason for contamination is not known, SIAM said in its now-withdrawn letter it had seen an increase in chloride levels since the rollout of E20 and has requested the government to direct oil marketing companies to find the root cause.

For moisture, the SIAM letter noted, the cause could be inadequate “maintenance of the underground storage tanks and pipelines at retail outlets”.

Maruti’s Bhat wrote in his July 26 email that 1 ppm of chloride was the maximum that current fuel injectors, which transport fuel to the engine, “can tolerate”.

“Lesser than 1 ppm in E20 is also in line with international standards. Same is in line with discussion held with” the petroleum ministry, Bhat wrote.

Mahindra’s senior principal engineer of fluids technology, R. Ramaprabhu, said in emails that organic chloride is the contaminant responsible for the very rapid vehicle failures the industry is seeing and can spoil engines “within 200km”.

“Majority cases reported immediately after fuelling … is due to organic chloride,” he wrote, adding that Mahindra has “strong evidences” of fuel sample data from retail outlets.

Mahindra’s Ramaprabhu and Maruti’s Bhat did not respond to Reuters’ queries.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Re0.94, raises high-speed diesel by Re0.54
World.content:
The government on Wednesday reduced the price of petrol by Re0.94 and increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.54 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs324.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs382.79 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 13 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: 'We aspire for it to grow': Turkiye's Erdogan eyes expansion of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
World.content:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Wednesday that he hoped more countries would join a defence agreement signed last week between Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, aimed at stabilising a region wracked by conflict.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed last week as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Iran war, which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

“Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily.

“Rather we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.”

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday.

Cairo has robust military cooperation with Ankara, but has given no indication it intends to sign up to the new security alliance, which contains a Nato-style clause saying any attack on one would be seen as an attack on all.

The five-month US-Iran war has upended the security architecture in the region and forced a rethink of decades of conventional wisdom rooted in US military supremacy.

Erdogan said the pact emerged out of the “new circumstances” in the Middle East with regional players seeking to assume greater responsibility for their own security and stability.

“Regional issues should be resolved by regional actors, and with this action, we consider that we have taken a first step toward achieving that goal,” he told the Saudi-owned newspaper.

“Resolving regional issues must be carried out away from formulas imposed from the outside. We know very well that solutions imported from abroad only bring disasters.”

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”.

Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

On Monday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif affirmed that the defence pact was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression.

Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

Israel ‘removing Palestine’ from world agenda

Erdogan also accused the Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu of seeking to “remove Palestine” from the world’s agenda.

“The aim of the Netanyahu government is to remove Palestine from the common agenda of humanity by profiting from chaos and new conflicts in the region,” Erdogan said at a joint news conference with his Palestinian counterpart, Mahmoud Abbas.

“No matter what they do, they will not succeed. The Palestinian cause will continue to grow in people’s hearts as they try to destroy it,” he stressed, vowing Turkiye would fight for the establishment of a Palestinian state.

A strong advocate of the Palestinian cause, Erdogan has repeatedly lambasted Netanyahu’s government, accusing the Israeli prime minister of committing “genocide” in Gaza and of pursuing expansionist policies in the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and beyond.

Abbas arrived in Ankara on Tuesday accompanied by his diplomatic adviser Majdi Khalidi, intelligence chief Majed Faraj and senior Palestinian official Ziad Abu Amr.

He met Erdogan on Wednesday with the pair discussing developments in the region in talks the Palestinian leader described as “important and fruitful”.

“I hope the decision to hold legislative and presidential elections in Palestine after a long time will bring good fortune … [and] will advance the reconciliation process,” Erdogan said, in a nod to the historic rivalry between Abbas’ Fatah movement and Gaza’s Hamas rulers.

Abbas also hailed the defence pact between Ankara, Riyadh and Islamabad, saying it was “of utmost importance” and expressing hope it would help enhance security and stability in the region.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength.
